records.content: 百龄坛 17 年 百龄坛旗下的 17 年调和苏格兰威士忌，酒液陈年至少 17 年，常见 40% vol；以 Glenburgie、Miltonduff、Glentauchers 三家酒厂的麦芽为风格骨架，呈蜂蜜、香草与柔和烟熏。 百龄坛 17 年 百龄坛 17 年是保乐力加旗下、由 Chivas Brothers 经营的调和苏格兰威士忌，酒液陈年至少 17 年，常见酒精度 40% vol。它最容易被误解的一点，是把“17 年”当成一次简单的年份加法；实际上，这个年份在品牌官方年表里可以追到 1937 年，是调酒师 George Robertson 为百龄坛定下的一个独立产品档位。 百龄坛 17 年 栏目示意图 图：百龄坛 17 年栏目示意图。项目自产或类别插图，用于威士忌类别语境，不是该对象的实拍。 1937 年：17 年这个年份的来历 百龄坛官方年表记载，George Robertson 于 1937 年加入品牌，并在任内做出品牌称为“世界第一款”的 17 年苏格兰威士忌，同时还留下了 30 年产品。这段叙述属于品牌自述，但它解释了一个产品逻辑：17 年不是从 12 年“顺延”出来的，而是百龄坛在 20 世纪上半叶就主动占住的一个中间年份。今天这瓶酒的法定含义仍然朴素——瓶中每一部分酒液都至少陈年 17 年，不是平均 17 年，也不是调和完成后再放 17 年。 爱丁堡 Cowgate 的杂货店（1827） George Ballantine 生于 1809 年，19 岁时在爱丁堡 Cowgate 开出一家杂货店，官方把 1827 年记为品牌起点。1836 年，他开始把精选麦芽

records.title: 芝华士 18 年
records.summary: 芝华士旗下的 18 年调和苏格兰威士忌，1997 年由 Colin Scott 推出、2004 年定名 Gold Signature；常见 40% vol，以 Strathisla 麦芽为骨架，呈干果、黑巧克力与肉桂。 芝华士 18 年 芝华士 18 年是保乐力加旗下芝华士的 18 年调和苏格兰威士忌，常见酒精度 40
records.content: 芝华士 18 年 芝华士旗下的 18 年调和苏格兰威士忌，1997 年由 Colin Scott 推出、2004 年定名 Gold Signature；常见 40% vol，以 Strathisla 麦芽为骨架，呈干果、黑巧克力与肉桂。 芝华士 18 年 芝华士 18 年是保乐力加旗下芝华士的 18 年调和苏格兰威士忌，常见酒精度 40% vol。它并不是 1909 年那瓶“世界第一款奢侈威士忌”的自然延续，而是 1997 年由当时的首席调酒师 Colin Scott 补上的中间档位：往上接 25 年，往下接 12 年。 芝华士 18 年 栏目示意图 图：芝华士 18 年栏目示意图。项目自产或类别插图，用于威士忌类别语境，不是该对象的实拍。 1997 年：18 年补上的中间档 芝华士官方在 Colin Scott 退休报道中确认：Chivas 18 Gold Signature 于 1997 年推出，2004 年换装时把他的金色签名放上瓶身。Colin Scott 1973 年进入 Chivas Brothers，1989 年成为品牌第五任首席调酒师。这条时间线解释了 18 年的定位——它不是把 12 年简单加六年，而是在 12 年与 25 年之间建立一个更易进入的高年份产品。这也解释了为什么 18 年的官方风味描述比 12 年更厚：它需要在中间档位撑起一套独立的品鉴语言，而不是只做“更贵的 12 年”。 Strathisla：1786 年的石墙 芝华士的家是 Strathisla 酒厂。官方资料把它记为 1786 年创立、苏格兰高地仍在运转的最古老酒厂，并明确说 Strath

records.title: 拉弗格 10 年
records.summary: 苏格兰艾雷岛的单一麦芽威士忌，以泥煤烘麦与海洋气息著称，在波本桶中陈年至少 10 年；常见 40% vol（部分市场为 43% vol），700 mL。 拉弗格 10 年 拉弗格 10 年是苏格兰艾雷岛南岸的单一麦芽威士忌，以泥煤烘麦带来的烟熏、碘酒与海洋气息著称，在波本桶中陈年至少 10 年，常见 40% vol、7
records.content: 拉弗格 10 年 苏格兰艾雷岛的单一麦芽威士忌，以泥煤烘麦与海洋气息著称，在波本桶中陈年至少 10 年；常见 40% vol（部分市场为 43% vol），700 mL。 拉弗格 10 年 拉弗格 10 年是苏格兰艾雷岛南岸的单一麦芽威士忌，以泥煤烘麦带来的烟熏、碘酒与海洋气息著称，在波本桶中陈年至少 10 年，常见 40% vol、700 mL，部分市场标注 43% vol。 拉弗格 10 年相关实景照片 图：拉弗格 10 年相关实景照片。图片：JIP，CC BY-SA 3.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 先分层：威士忌是大类，苏格兰单一麦芽是法定类型，艾雷岛是产区，拉弗格是酒厂与品牌，10 年是具体产品的年份标注。四层分开看，才不会把海岛风格、酒厂工艺与瓶中酒龄混为一谈。 “10 年”是法定年份标注，指瓶中所有酒液的最低陈年时间。它属于酒厂的常规入门款，之上还有 18 年、25 年与桶强版本；入门款不代表低质，它更像酒厂风格的“基准线”。 生产者与品牌 拉弗格酒厂于 1815 年由唐纳德·约翰斯顿与亚历山大·约翰斯顿在艾雷岛南岸建立，长期由家族经营，现属三得利控股旗下的 Beam Suntory。酒厂是艾雷岛泥煤风格的代表性生产者之一。 酒厂、品牌与产品是三个层级：酒厂回答设备与工艺，品牌回答定位与产品线，产品回答年份、桶型与酒精度。企业所有权可能随集团调整，购买时仍以标签上的装瓶商与实际信息为准。 「拉弗格 10 年」的产地与原料 艾雷岛位于苏格兰西岸，属海洋性气候，风大、湿度高、温差小，酒厂多临海而建。当地泥煤由植物残体堆积而成

records.title: 麦卡伦12年
records.summary: 苏格兰斯佩赛产区的单一麦芽威士忌，以雪莉风味桶陈酿为特色，酒龄标注为 12 年；常见 700 mL 或 750 mL、酒精度约 40% vol，具体版本与批次以瓶标为准。 麦卡伦12年 麦卡伦12年（The Macallan 12）是苏格兰斯佩赛产区的单一麦芽威士忌，以雪莉风味桶陈酿为特色，酒龄标注为 12 年。常见
records.content: 麦卡伦12年 苏格兰斯佩赛产区的单一麦芽威士忌，以雪莉风味桶陈酿为特色，酒龄标注为 12 年；常见 700 mL 或 750 mL、酒精度约 40% vol，具体版本与批次以瓶标为准。 麦卡伦12年 麦卡伦12年（The Macallan 12）是苏格兰斯佩赛产区的单一麦芽威士忌，以雪莉风味桶陈酿为特色，酒龄标注为 12 年。常见 700 mL 或 750 mL 瓶装、酒精度约 40% vol，具体版本、桶型与批次以瓶标为准。 麦卡伦12年相关实景照片 图：麦卡伦12年相关实景照片。图片：Ssu，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 麦卡伦12年是一个具体产品，不是麦卡伦品牌的统称。它属于单一麦芽威士忌：同一家蒸馏厂生产，原料为水与发芽大麦，不使用其他酒厂的调和基酒。品牌下还有不同酒龄与不同桶型的版本，定位与价格不同。 酒龄标注是瓶中最年轻原酒的年龄，不是平均年龄，也不是装瓶后的年份。12 年代表最低酒龄为 12 年，实际可能包含更老的酒液；判断具体风味仍要看桶型、版本与批次。 「麦卡伦12年」的产地与原料 斯佩赛位于苏格兰东北部，是苏格兰威士忌的重要产区，酒厂多沿河分布。当地水源与气候影响糖化、发酵与陈酿条件；斯佩赛风格常被描述为偏花果与柔和，但不同酒厂差异明显。 原料为水、发芽大麦与酵母。大麦发芽后经烘干，部分工艺使用泥煤，泥煤用量影响烟熏风味。麦卡伦通常不以重泥煤为特色，风味更多来自桶型与陈酿。 糖化与发酵 就「麦卡伦12年」而言，糖化把麦芽中的淀粉转化为可发酵糖，温度与时间影响提取效率与糖分组成。发酵把糖转化为酒

records.title: 麦卡伦18年雪莉桶
records.summary: 苏格兰斯佩塞单一麦芽威士忌，1824 年创立；雪莉调味橡木桶陈年，18 年款常见酒精度 43% vol。 麦卡伦18年雪莉桶 麦卡伦（The Macallan）是苏格兰斯佩塞（Speyside）产区的单一麦芽威士忌品牌，1824 年创立于克雷盖拉希（Craigellachie）。麦卡伦 18 年雪莉桶以雪莉调味橡木桶陈
records.content: 麦卡伦18年雪莉桶 苏格兰斯佩塞单一麦芽威士忌，1824 年创立；雪莉调味橡木桶陈年，18 年款常见酒精度 43% vol。 麦卡伦18年雪莉桶 麦卡伦（The Macallan）是苏格兰斯佩塞（Speyside）产区的单一麦芽威士忌品牌，1824 年创立于克雷盖拉希（Craigellachie）。麦卡伦 18 年雪莉桶以雪莉调味橡木桶陈年风格著称，常见酒精度为 43% vol。风味以葡萄干、无花果、橙皮、丁香与黑巧克力为主。 麦卡伦18年雪莉桶 栏目示意图 图：麦卡伦18年雪莉桶栏目示意图。项目自产或类别插图，用于威士忌类别语境，不是该对象的实拍。 定义与身份 单一麦芽威士忌指同一家蒸馏厂用 100% 发芽大麦生产、并在该厂陈年的威士忌。它不意味着“单一桶”，也不意味着“单一年份”。麦卡伦 18 年是多个橡木桶调配后的产品；“18 年”表示瓶中酒液的最低陈年时间，而不是某一桶的准确年龄。 “雪莉桶”在威士忌行业通常指用雪莉酒润桶或经过雪莉酒 seasoning 的橡木桶，而不是把雪莉酒直接加入威士忌。桶的来源、润桶方式、使用次数与陈年环境，都会影响干果、香料与木质风味的强度。标签写“雪莉桶”说明风格方向，不等于每一滴酒都来自同一种桶。 「麦卡伦18年雪莉桶」的时间线 1824 年，Alexander Reid 在斯佩塞的 Easter Elchies 一带取得蒸馏许可，建立后来的麦卡伦蒸馏厂。19 世纪末至 20 世纪，酒厂经历所有权变更与扩建，逐渐把“雪莉桶陈年”作为核心风格。20 世纪后期，麦卡伦在国际拍卖与高端市场中获得较高知名度，成为单一麦芽威士忌的代表品牌之一。 品

records.title: 西凤酒
records.summary: 产自陕西凤翔的凤香型白酒代表，以高粱为原料、土暗窖发酵、酒海贮存，常见酒精度 55% vol。 西凤酒 西凤酒产自陕西凤翔，是凤香型白酒的代表。它以高粱为原料，大麦、小麦、豌豆制曲，采用土暗窖发酵、酒海贮存，常见酒精度为 55% vol。 西凤酒 图像 西凤酒。图片：Lhzss8，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wi
records.content: 西凤酒 产自陕西凤翔的凤香型白酒代表，以高粱为原料、土暗窖发酵、酒海贮存，常见酒精度 55% vol。 西凤酒 西凤酒产自陕西凤翔，是凤香型白酒的代表。它以高粱为原料，大麦、小麦、豌豆制曲，采用土暗窖发酵、酒海贮存，常见酒精度为 55% vol。 西凤酒 图像 图：西凤酒。图片：Lhzss8，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 西凤酒是白酒中的一个品牌，也是凤香型的主要代表。凤香型的定位介于清香与浓香之间：它既有清香型的爽净，也带有浓香型的窖香与醇厚。它不是“清香加浓香”的简单混合，而是一套独立的制曲、发酵与贮存传统。 产品属于蒸馏酒，酒精度以体积分数标示，常见为 55% vol。高度版本对饮用方式更敏感，比较时也不能只看度数。 产区与环境 凤翔位于陕西关中西部，属暖温带大陆性季风气候，四季分明、降水集中，空气相对干燥。干燥环境有利于制曲与贮存，也影响窖池微生物的季节变化。当地高粱与水源，是凤香风格的基础条件。 西凤酒使用土暗窖发酵，窖池与泥窖的微生物环境不同，带来的香气结构也不同。窖池需要长期维护，窖泥状态会随使用与季节变化。产区风格不是单靠地名形成的，它是气候、窖池、原料与工艺共同积累的结果。 凤翔古称雍，是关中西部的重要城邑，酿酒传统与当地农业、商贸长期相连。西凤酒在近代经历了从作坊到工厂的转变，酒海贮存等传统环节在部分产品中被保留下来。 原料与制曲 主料是高粱，要求颗粒饱满、淀粉含量高、杂质少。曲以大麦、小麦与豌豆为原料，不同曲种的配比与培菌温度会影响糖化力与香气前体。制曲是凤香型风格的基础环节，曲香过重会掩盖

records.title: 张裕葡萄酒
records.summary: 山东烟台葡萄酒品牌，张裕公司创建于 1892 年，产品覆盖干红、干白与白兰地，常用蛇龙珠、赤霞珠、霞多丽等品种。 张裕葡萄酒 张裕葡萄酒产自山东烟台。张裕公司创建于 1892 年，创办人为张弼士，是中国最早的现代葡萄酒企业之一。产品覆盖干红、干白、白兰地等，常用品种包括蛇龙珠、赤霞珠和霞多丽。 张裕葡萄酒实景照片 张裕
records.content: 张裕葡萄酒 山东烟台葡萄酒品牌，张裕公司创建于 1892 年，产品覆盖干红、干白与白兰地，常用蛇龙珠、赤霞珠、霞多丽等品种。 张裕葡萄酒 张裕葡萄酒产自山东烟台。张裕公司创建于 1892 年，创办人为张弼士，是中国最早的现代葡萄酒企业之一。产品覆盖干红、干白、白兰地等，常用品种包括蛇龙珠、赤霞珠和霞多丽。 张裕葡萄酒实景照片 图：张裕葡萄酒。摄影：Guang Lu Di in Dabu. Built in 1908, former residence of Cheong Fatt Tze who was the founder of Changyu Wine (19324457523)。署名：Yun Huang Yong from Harbord, Australia，CC BY 2.0，来自 Wikimedia Commons（来源）。 定义与定位 张裕既是企业名称，也是葡萄酒品牌。它不是一个产区，也不是某一个葡萄品种。把它当作葡萄酒品牌来理解，才能正确区分“张裕”与“烟台产区”“蛇龙珠品种”这些不同层级的概念。 张裕的业务并不限于葡萄酒，还包括白兰地等蒸馏酒产品。本页只讨论其葡萄酒部分。企业历史长、产品线宽，意味着同一品牌下不同系列的价格、工艺与风格差异可能很大，单看品牌名不足以判断一瓶酒的实际定位。 产区与环境 烟台位于山东半岛北部，北临渤海、东临黄海，属暖温带季风气候，受海洋调节明显：春季回暖较慢，夏季不算酷热，秋季相对漫长。葡萄生长季温和，成熟期的海风与昼夜温差影响糖酸平衡。 海洋性气候带来较高湿度，也带来病害压力，需要更细致的树体管理与采收判断。烟台是中国重要的葡萄

records.title: 即墨老酒
records.summary: 山东即墨出产的黄酒，以黍米与麦曲酿制，沿用“古遗六法”的传统工艺；常见 500 mL 瓶装、酒精度约 12% vol，糖分类型与年份以瓶标为准。 即墨老酒 即墨老酒是山东即墨出产的黄酒，以黍米与麦曲酿制，沿用被称为“古遗六法”的传统工艺。常见 500 mL 瓶装、酒精度约 12% vol，糖分类型、年份与批次以瓶标为准
records.content: 即墨老酒 山东即墨出产的黄酒，以黍米与麦曲酿制，沿用“古遗六法”的传统工艺；常见 500 mL 瓶装、酒精度约 12% vol，糖分类型与年份以瓶标为准。 即墨老酒 即墨老酒是山东即墨出产的黄酒，以黍米与麦曲酿制，沿用被称为“古遗六法”的传统工艺。常见 500 mL 瓶装、酒精度约 12% vol，糖分类型、年份与批次以瓶标为准。 即墨老酒类别配图 图：即墨老酒所属的黄酒类别配图。图片：udono，CC BY-SA 2.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是即墨老酒的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 即墨老酒是一个具体的黄酒产品，也是山东即墨一带黄酒传统的代表名称之一。它属于中国黄酒体系，与绍兴黄酒同属米酒大类，但原料、曲种与风味路线不同：绍兴黄酒多用糯米与麦曲，即墨老酒以黍米为原料，风味更偏向焦香与醇厚。 黄酒是发酵酒，不是蒸馏酒。它与白酒的区别不仅在酒精度，还在原料处理、发酵方式与饮用场景。即墨老酒常被用作饮用、烹饪与调制，具体用途取决于产品等级与糖分类型。 「即墨老酒」的产地与原料 即墨位于山东半岛西南部，气候温和，水源与粮食供应为黄酒生产提供了条件。当地黄酒传统与北方饮食结构相互影响，形成了偏醇厚、偏焦香的风格路线。 原料以黍米为主，搭配麦曲与水。黍米提供淀粉与风味物质，麦曲提供糖化与发酵所需的酶与微生物。水的质量对黄酒风味影响明显，传统工艺强调水源洁净。原料的品种与等级会影响成品风格，具体配方属于企业工艺信息。 古遗六法 “古遗六法”是即墨老酒常被引用的传统工艺表述，强调黍米、曲蘖、水泉、陶器、清洁与火候六个环节。它描

records.title: 青岛啤酒
records.summary: 产自山东青岛的拉格啤酒品牌，1903 年创办，主力产品酒精度约 4% vol，是中国历史最久的啤酒品牌之一。 青岛啤酒 青岛啤酒产自山东青岛，是中国历史最久的啤酒品牌之一，1903 年由德英商人创办。主力产品为下面发酵的拉格啤酒，常见酒精度约 4% vol。 青岛啤酒 图像 青岛啤酒。图片：Lennartbj，CC B
records.content: 青岛啤酒 产自山东青岛的拉格啤酒品牌，1903 年创办，主力产品酒精度约 4% vol，是中国历史最久的啤酒品牌之一。 青岛啤酒 青岛啤酒产自山东青岛，是中国历史最久的啤酒品牌之一，1903 年由德英商人创办。主力产品为下面发酵的拉格啤酒，常见酒精度约 4% vol。 青岛啤酒 图像 图：青岛啤酒。图片：Lennartbj，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 青岛啤酒是品牌与企业名称，产品属于啤酒中的拉格。它不是“中国版德国啤酒”的简单复制，而是德式酿造技术在中国落地后，结合本地原料与市场形成的工业啤酒体系。 需要区分品牌与产品线：经典、纯生、白啤、黑啤等系列风格不同，酒精度、原麦汁浓度与原料也有差异。用一个描述概括整个品牌并不准确，具体产品应以标签为准。 产地与环境 青岛位于山东半岛南岸，濒临黄海，属温带季风气候，受海洋调节，夏季温和、冬季较冷，空气湿润。优质水源是早期选址的重要因素，崂山一带的水源长期被用于酿造。 港口与铁路条件也影响了青岛啤酒的早期发展：德占时期建设的交通与工业基础，使啤酒得以规模化生产与外销。产地优势是历史与工业条件的结果，不等于每一瓶都在同一厂区生产；具体产地应看标签。 青岛的港口条件使大麦、酒花等原料的进口与成品外运更为便利，这是早期工业啤酒布局的区位优势。今天企业在全国多地设厂，产地与品牌已不再一一对应，消费者应关注标签上的生产厂址。 原料 主要原料包括大麦芽、水、酒花与酵母。部分产品使用大米或淀粉类辅料以调整成本与风味，这是工业拉格的常见做法；辅料比例会影响麦芽香与酒体厚度。酒花提供苦味

records.title: 汾酒
records.summary: 产自山西汾阳杏花村的清香型白酒代表，以高粱、大麦和豌豆制曲，常见酒精度 53% vol。 汾酒 汾酒产自山西汾阳杏花村，是清香型白酒的代表。它以高粱为原料，大麦和豌豆制曲，采用清蒸二次清工艺，常见酒精度为 53% vol。 汾酒 图像 汾酒。图片：N509FZ，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Co
records.content: 汾酒 产自山西汾阳杏花村的清香型白酒代表，以高粱、大麦和豌豆制曲，常见酒精度 53% vol。 汾酒 汾酒产自山西汾阳杏花村，是清香型白酒的代表。它以高粱为原料，大麦和豌豆制曲，采用清蒸二次清工艺，常见酒精度为 53% vol。 汾酒 图像 图：汾酒。图片：N509FZ，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面.jpg)）。 定义与定位 汾酒是白酒中的一个品牌，也是清香型白酒的典型代表。清香型的“清”指工艺上的清蒸清烧与地缸发酵，也指风味上的干净、爽净。它与浓香、酱香不是同一套评价体系，风格差异不应被简化为质量高低。 产品属于蒸馏酒，酒精度以体积分数标示，常见为 53% vol。不同系列与度数会改变入口刺激与香气释放，但都应以标签为准。 产区与环境 杏花村位于山西汾阳，属于温带大陆性季风气候，四季分明、降水较少，空气相对干燥。干燥气候有利于制曲与贮存，也减少了开放式发酵中杂菌的风险。当地水源与高粱品质，是清香风格的重要条件。 清香型白酒使用地缸发酵，而不是泥窖。缸体埋入地下，酒醅与土壤隔离，发酵环境更干净，窖泥带来的复合香气较少。这样的工艺选择，直接决定了清香型“净”的风格取向，也解释了它与浓香型在香气结构上的根本差异。 杏花村的酿酒传统在明清时期随晋商贸易向外扩散，清香工艺也影响了北方多地的白酒生产。讨论汾酒时，既要看历史传承，也要看具体产品的原料与工艺执行，不能只凭产地叙事下结论。 原料与制曲 主料是高粱，要求颗粒饱满、淀粉含量高。辅料为谷壳，用于调整酒醅的疏松度与含氧量。曲以大麦和豌豆为原料，通常包括清茬曲、后火曲与红心曲等类型，不同

records.title: 智慧舍得
records.summary: 舍得酒业旗下的高端浓香型单品，2018 年上市，常见 52% vol、42% vol 或 38% vol、500 mL；企业公开资料称以贮存八年以上基酒并用陈酒调味。 智慧舍得 “智慧舍得”是舍得品牌旗下定位较高的浓香型单品，2018 年上市，常见规格为 52% vol、42% vol 或 38% vol、500 mL
records.content: 智慧舍得 舍得酒业旗下的高端浓香型单品，2018 年上市，常见 52% vol、42% vol 或 38% vol、500 mL；企业公开资料称以贮存八年以上基酒并用陈酒调味。 智慧舍得 “智慧舍得”是舍得品牌旗下定位较高的浓香型单品，2018 年上市，常见规格为 52% vol、42% vol 或 38% vol、500 mL，产自四川射洪。它把“老酒”与“文化”放在同一个产品叙事里，理解时需要把品牌、生产者、基酒来源与具体规格分开看。 智慧舍得类别配图 图：智慧舍得所属的白酒类别配图。图片：Xiaomage de，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是智慧舍得的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 智慧舍得属于舍得品牌的核心战略单品，位置高于流通面较广的品味舍得，承担商务宴请与礼赠场景。它仍是浓香型白酒，不是独立香型，也不是“年份酒”的法定等级。 产品名中的“智慧”来自品牌的文化表述，不是质量等级；“舍得”既是品牌名也是产品名，交流时要加上系列名才能指向具体一瓶酒。 生产者与品牌 酒款由舍得酒业股份有限公司组织生产，品牌由舍得承载。企业位于四川射洪沱牌镇，前身可溯至 1940 年泰安作坊，1952 年设国营沱牌曲酒厂，1993 年注册股份公司，1996 年上市。 2001 年 12 月，企业在沱牌曲酒的基础上推出舍得品牌，面向高端市场；2018 年 1 月公司更名为舍得酒业股份有限公司。品牌与股份公司是两个层级，前者是市场标识，后者是法律主体。 「智慧舍得」的产地与原料 射洪位于四川盆地中部，涪江流域，气候

records.title: 剑南春
records.summary: 产自四川绵竹的浓香型白酒，以五粮为原料、泥窖固态发酵，常见酒精度 52% vol。 剑南春 剑南春产自四川绵竹，属浓香型白酒。它以高粱、大米、糯米、小麦、玉米为原料，采用泥窖固态发酵、续糟配料等传统工艺，常见酒精度为 52% vol。 剑南春实景照片 剑南春。摄影：剑南春酒坊遗址国保碑。署名：Nekitarc，CC B
records.content: 剑南春 产自四川绵竹的浓香型白酒，以五粮为原料、泥窖固态发酵，常见酒精度 52% vol。 剑南春 剑南春产自四川绵竹，属浓香型白酒。它以高粱、大米、糯米、小麦、玉米为原料，采用泥窖固态发酵、续糟配料等传统工艺，常见酒精度为 52% vol。 剑南春实景照片 图：剑南春。摄影：剑南春酒坊遗址国保碑。署名：Nekitarc，CC BY-SA 4.0，来自 Wikimedia Commons（来源）。 定义与定位 剑南春是白酒中的一个品牌，也是浓香型白酒的代表之一。它采用五粮配方，但风格与川南的浓香酒并不完全相同：绵竹位于四川盆地西北边缘，气候、水源与窖池条件形成了自己的路线。 产品属于蒸馏酒，酒精度以体积分数标示，常见为 52% vol。不同系列与年份的酒体设计不同，比较时应先确认产品线，而不是只看品牌名。 产区与环境 绵竹位于成都平原西北缘，靠近龙门山，气候比川南更温和，昼夜温差与湿度条件不同。当地水源与空气微生物影响制曲与发酵，也影响窖池中微生物群落的构成。产区风格不是单一因素决定，而是气候、粮食与工艺共同作用。 绵竹的酿酒传统与当地农业、商贸长期相连。地名能提示产区，但不能替代对具体产品的原料、窖池与勾调的核对。 剑南春的老窖池群是重要的生产资产。泥窖连续使用会让窖泥中的产香微生物逐渐稳定，形成更成熟的己酸菌生态。窖池需要维护，窖泥的酸碱度、水分与营养状态都会影响下一轮发酵，因此“老窖”背后是长期管理，而不是单纯的年份数字。 原料与制曲 五种粮食各有分工：高粱提供骨架，大米与糯米带来甜润与饱满，小麦提供曲香与发酵力，玉米增加甜味与厚度。原料粉碎后按比例混合，进入蒸煮与续糟配

records.title: 郎酒
records.summary: 产自四川古蔺赤水河畔的白酒品牌，兼有酱香与浓香产品；青花郎、红花郎是酱香主线，郎牌特曲等覆盖浓香与宴席场景，产地与茅台镇隔河相望。 郎酒 郎酒产自四川古蔺二郎镇，位于赤水河畔，产品兼有酱香型和浓香型，其中青花郎等酱香产品较为知名。常见酱香产品酒精度为 53% vol。 郎酒类别配图 郎酒所属的白酒类别配图。图片：Xia
records.content: 郎酒 产自四川古蔺赤水河畔的白酒品牌，兼有酱香与浓香产品；青花郎、红花郎是酱香主线，郎牌特曲等覆盖浓香与宴席场景，产地与茅台镇隔河相望。 郎酒 郎酒产自四川古蔺二郎镇，位于赤水河畔，产品兼有酱香型和浓香型，其中青花郎等酱香产品较为知名。常见酱香产品酒精度为 53% vol。 郎酒类别配图 图：郎酒所属的白酒类别配图。图片：Xiaomage de，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是郎酒的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 郎酒是白酒中的一个品牌，产品线横跨酱香与浓香两种风格。品牌名、香型与产地需要分开看：二郎镇是产地，郎酒是品牌，酱香或浓香是工艺与风味类别。同属赤水河谷，也不意味着所有产品都是同一种香型。 酱香产品属于蒸馏酒，酒精度以体积分数标示，常见为 53% vol。不同产品线的度数、酒体与勾调目标不同，比较时应先确认香型，再谈风格。 产区与环境 二郎镇位于赤水河中游，河谷深切、湿度较高，夏季炎热，冬季相对温和。这样的气候有利于开放式制曲、堆积发酵与长期贮存中的微生物活动。当地水源与河谷空气被视为酱香风格的环境条件之一。 郎酒的一大特点是利用天然溶洞贮存基酒。溶洞内温度与湿度相对稳定，陶坛中的酒液在较恒定的环境中缓慢变化。洞藏不是神秘化概念，它本质上是一种贮存环境管理；效果仍取决于基酒质量、容器与时间。 赤水河谷的水质与紫色砂页岩地层，常被当地酒业视为酿造条件。这类说法有地域经验基础，但不宜当作唯一解释；原料、曲、窖池与勾调同样决定成品风格。 原料与制曲 酱香产品以高粱为原料，用小麦制作高温大曲。高粱需

records.title: 泸州老窖
records.summary: 产自四川泸州的浓香型白酒代表，以老窖池续糟发酵为特色，常见产品酒精度 52% vol。 泸州老窖 泸州老窖产自四川泸州，是浓香型白酒的代表之一。其老窖池群连续使用时间长，“续糟配料、混蒸混烧”的泥窖固态发酵形成窖香浓郁的风格，常见产品酒精度为 52% vol。 泸州老窖 图像 泸州老窖。图片：Xiaomage de，C
records.content: 泸州老窖 产自四川泸州的浓香型白酒代表，以老窖池续糟发酵为特色，常见产品酒精度 52% vol。 泸州老窖 泸州老窖产自四川泸州，是浓香型白酒的代表之一。其老窖池群连续使用时间长，“续糟配料、混蒸混烧”的泥窖固态发酵形成窖香浓郁的风格，常见产品酒精度为 52% vol。 泸州老窖 图像 图：泸州老窖。图片：Xiaomage de，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 泸州老窖是白酒中的一个品牌，也是浓香型白酒的典型代表。品牌名中的“老窖”指向泥窖长期连续使用这一工艺事实：窖池不是一次性容器，而是持续参与发酵的微生物栖息地。理解这一点，才能理解浓香型白酒为何强调窖池年龄。 产品属于蒸馏酒，酒精度以体积分数标示，常见为 52% vol，也有低度版本。不同产品的酒体设计与勾调目标不同，不能只按度数比较。 产区与环境 泸州位于四川南部，长江与沱江在此交汇，气候温暖湿润，适合开放式制曲与长期窖池发酵。当地水源、粮食与空气微生物共同构成酿造环境。浓香型白酒的产区风格，往往与窖池群的历史、原料供应和气候条件绑定。 泸州老窖的老窖池群被视为重要的酿造遗产。窖池连续使用时间越长，窖泥中的微生物生态越稳定，产香能力越成熟。需要说明的是，“窖池越老酒越好”是经验判断，具体产品仍取决于原料、工艺控制与勾调。 原料与制曲 泸州老窖以高粱为主要原料，属于单粮浓香路线。高粱提供淀粉与适量单宁，单宁在发酵中转化，带来结构感与回味。原料粉碎后与曲、水配合，进入续糟配料流程。 曲以小麦为主，经培菌制成中高温大曲。制曲决定糖化力与香气前体，曲的质量直接影响出

records.title: 五粮液
records.summary: 产自四川宜宾的浓香型白酒，以高粱、大米、糯米、小麦、玉米五种粮食为原料，常见酒精度 52% vol。 五粮液 五粮液产自四川宜宾，以高粱、大米、糯米、小麦、玉米五种粮食为原料，属浓香型白酒。老窖池持续发酵、续糟配料和混蒸混烧是其主要工艺特征，常见产品酒精度为 52% vol。 五粮液 图像 五粮液。图片：东京村子，CC
records.content: 五粮液 产自四川宜宾的浓香型白酒，以高粱、大米、糯米、小麦、玉米五种粮食为原料，常见酒精度 52% vol。 五粮液 五粮液产自四川宜宾，以高粱、大米、糯米、小麦、玉米五种粮食为原料，属浓香型白酒。老窖池持续发酵、续糟配料和混蒸混烧是其主要工艺特征，常见产品酒精度为 52% vol。 五粮液 图像 图：五粮液。图片：东京村子，CC BY-SA 3.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 五粮液是白酒中的一个品牌产品，也是浓香型白酒的代表之一。它的名称直接指向原料结构：五种粮食混合酿造。品牌、香型与产地是不同层次的概念，选购时需要分别核对，不能把“宜宾产的浓香酒”都当成五粮液。 产品属于蒸馏酒，酒精度以体积分数标示，常见为 52% vol，也有 39% vol 等低度版本。度数差异会影响入口刺激与香气释放，但不构成质量高下。 产区与环境 宜宾位于四川南部，岷江与金沙江在此汇合后进入长江，河谷气候湿润、温差相对温和，适合开放式制曲与长期窖池发酵。当地水源与空气微生物被视为浓香风格的环境条件之一。产区优势不是单一因素，而是气候、粮食、窖池与工艺共同积累的结果。 老窖池是宜宾浓香酒的重要资产。窖池连续使用时间越长，窖泥中的微生物群落越稳定，己酸菌等产香微生物的生态越成熟。窖池不是容器那么简单，它参与风味形成，因此“老窖”在浓香型白酒中具有实际意义，而不只是营销词。 原料与制曲 五种粮食各有角色：高粱提供骨架与单宁带来的结构感，大米与糯米增加甜润与醇厚，小麦带来曲香与发酵力，玉米带来甜味与酒体厚度。比例不是固定不变，不同产品线会调整配比以形成风格差异。

records.title: 贝加西西里亚
records.summary: 西班牙杜埃罗河岸产区的历史名庄，1864 年创立；以丹魄为主的混酿，旗舰酒款 Único 以长陈年与复杂度著称，常见 750 mL、酒精度约 14% vol，具体年份与批次以瓶标为准。 贝加西西里亚 贝加西西里亚（Vega Sicilia）是西班牙杜埃罗河岸产区的历史名庄，1864 年创立。酒款属于红葡萄酒，以丹魄为主
records.content: 贝加西西里亚 西班牙杜埃罗河岸产区的历史名庄，1864 年创立；以丹魄为主的混酿，旗舰酒款 Único 以长陈年与复杂度著称，常见 750 mL、酒精度约 14% vol，具体年份与批次以瓶标为准。 贝加西西里亚 贝加西西里亚（Vega Sicilia）是西班牙杜埃罗河岸产区的历史名庄，1864 年创立。酒款属于红葡萄酒，以丹魄为主的混酿，旗舰酒款 Único 以长陈年与复杂度著称。常见 750 mL 瓶装、酒精度约 14% vol，具体年份、装瓶批次与酒标信息以瓶标为准。 贝加西西里亚 图像 图：贝加西西里亚。图片：Dominic Lockyer，CC BY 2.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 贝加西西里亚既是酒庄名，也是酒庄产品的品牌名。酒庄位于西班牙北部杜埃罗河岸产区，在欧盟 AOC/AOP 体系中以原产地命名销售。旗舰酒款 Único 之外还有 Valbuena 等产品，不同酒款来自不同地块与筛选标准，不能混为一谈。 在葡萄酒的分类里，它属于静态红葡萄酒。历史名庄是长期积累的市场身份，不是法定等级；年份、地块与装瓶批次仍然是判断具体酒款的前提。 产区与气候 杜埃罗河岸位于西班牙北部高原，海拔较高，气候大陆性明显：夏季炎热干燥，冬季寒冷，昼夜温差大。这样的条件适合丹魄等品种在较长的成熟期内积累风味，同时保留酸度。 产区土壤由石灰岩、黏土与砾石混合而成，不同地块的排水与升温条件不同。海拔与朝向影响成熟节奏，酒庄需要按地块分批采收。高海拔与大陆性气候不是质量保证，年份差异仍然明显。 品种与混酿 酒款以丹魄为主体，常搭配赤霞珠与其他品种

records.title: 绝对伏特加
records.summary: 瑞典伏特加品牌，以冬小麦为原料，在 Åhus 连续蒸馏；1979 年推出，常见酒精度 40% vol。 绝对伏特加 绝对伏特加（Absolut Vodka）是瑞典伏特加品牌，以冬小麦为原料，在瑞典南部斯科讷省的 Åhus 生产，采用连续蒸馏。品牌于 1979 年推出，常见酒精度为 40% vol，风味以干净、柔和的谷物
records.content: 绝对伏特加 瑞典伏特加品牌，以冬小麦为原料，在 Åhus 连续蒸馏；1979 年推出，常见酒精度 40% vol。 绝对伏特加 绝对伏特加（Absolut Vodka）是瑞典伏特加品牌，以冬小麦为原料，在瑞典南部斯科讷省的 Åhus 生产，采用连续蒸馏。品牌于 1979 年推出，常见酒精度为 40% vol，风味以干净、柔和的谷物甜感为主。 绝对伏特加实景照片 图：绝对伏特加。摄影：Absolut vodka bottle。署名：Justus Blümer，CC BY 3.0，来自 Wikimedia Commons（来源）。 定义与身份 伏特加是以农产品为原料、经蒸馏得到的高纯度酒精饮料，欧盟法规要求其装瓶酒精度不低于 37.5% vol。它可以是中性风味，也可以带有原料带来的轻微谷物或马铃薯特征。绝对伏特加属于“原味伏特加”，不是加味伏特加，也不是利口酒。 “绝对”既是品牌名，也是产品线的统称。品牌还有柠檬、柑橘、香草等加味版本，它们以原味伏特加为基酒再加入风味，不能与原味产品混为一谈。购买时应看标签上的版本名与酒精度，不能把某一款加味产品的甜度当成原味伏特加的特征。 「绝对伏特加」的时间线 Åhus 的蒸馏传统可以追溯到 1879 年，当地以小麦与水源为基础发展蒸馏业。1979 年，绝对伏特加作为面向国际市场的瑞典伏特加品牌推出，凭借简洁瓶身与广告设计迅速获得识别度。此后品牌扩展到多个国家，并推出不同风味与限量版本。 品牌所有权在 21 世纪发生变化，现由国际酒业集团持有。品牌在不同市场维持统一的原料与蒸馏标准，使产品风味相对稳定。历史年份与某一瓶酒的生产日期不是同一件事

records.content: 水井坊·典藏大师版 四川水井坊股份有限公司的高端浓香型单品，常见 52% vol 或 38% vol、500 mL；以水井街酒坊遗址与“第一坊”叙事为背景，定位商务与礼赠。 水井坊·典藏大师版 “水井坊·典藏大师版”是水井坊品牌高端产品线中的浓香型单品，公开资料常见的规格为 52% vol 与 38% vol、500 mL，产自四川成都。它把水井街酒坊遗址的历史叙事与高端价格带放在一起，理解时需要把品牌、生产者、遗址与具体规格分开看。 水井坊·典藏大师版类别配图 图：水井坊·典藏大师版所属的白酒类别配图。图片：Xiaomage de，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是水井坊·典藏大师版的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 典藏大师版处在水井坊产品线的高端位置，和菁翠、第一坊、井台与臻酿八号形成分层，主要面向商务宴请与礼赠。它仍是浓香型白酒，不是独立香型，也不是“年份酒”的法定等级。 “典藏大师版”是产品名，不是质量认证。公开报道把它描述为水井坊进攻高端的核心产品，这类市场表述说明价格带与渠道定位，不等于对酒体等级的独立评定。 生产者与品牌 酒款由四川水井坊股份有限公司组织生产，品牌由水井坊承载。该公司于 1996 年 12 月在上海证券交易所上市，母公司为四川成都水井坊集团有限公司，实际控制人为帝亚吉欧。 品牌与股份公司是两个层级：品牌回答“叫什么、面向谁”，股份公司回答“谁持有商标、谁承担法律责任”。水井坊同时是公司名、品牌名与产品名，讨论具体风味时要先指明系列。 产区与遗址 水井坊位于成都平原，岷江流

records.content: 塔牌本酒 塔牌“本系列”的核心产品，500 mL 礼盒、15% vol、半干型，明确不添加焦糖色；产自绍兴柯桥区湖塘，以糯米、麦曲与鉴湖水手工酿造，与同厂本原酒、普通加饭酒是三个不同层级的产品。 塔牌本酒 塔牌本酒是塔牌“本系列”里最核心的一支：500 mL 礼盒、15% vol、半干型，商品页明确写“不添加焦糖色”。“本酒”是浙江塔牌绍兴酒有限公司给产品起的名字，不是国家标准里的等级，也不是“原浆”“基酒”的同义词。把它和同厂的本原酒、普通加饭酒分开看，才不会买错。 塔牌本酒类别配图 图：塔牌本酒所属的黄酒类别配图。图片：udono，CC BY-SA 2.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是塔牌本酒的产品、包装或门店实拍。 “本酒”是塔牌的产品名，不是国标术语 GB/T 17946 把绍兴酒按总糖分成元红、加饭（花雕）、善酿、香雪四类，没有“本酒”这一项。塔牌把“本”解释为“本色、本香、本味、本地、本人”，强调的是少修饰、保留发酵本来的颜色与香气。这个解释来自企业，不是标准的定义。所以本酒属于黄酒大类下的绍兴酒，具体归类要看瓶标上的糖分类型，通常落在半干型。 湖塘、1994 与出口底色 塔牌厂区在绍兴柯桥区湖塘街道，官网自述“位于鉴湖之源、中国黄酒产业基地”。企业 1994 年由浙江省粮油食品进出口股份有限公司投资兴建，占地 450 亩，有 13 个黄酒酿造车间、2 个瓶酒灌装车间、800 余名员工。官网还给出几个可核对的身份：68 年出口品牌、距鉴湖源头 500 米、3 位国家级大师，以及“全国最大纯手工酿造黄酒生产企业”的

records.content: 塔牌手工冬酿 塔牌以立冬到立春的低温窗口手工酿造的绍兴黄酒系列，按三年、五年、六年、八年、十年分档；产自绍兴柯桥区湖塘，以糯米、麦曲与鉴湖水为原料，落缸 26–30℃、总发酵期约 70–80 天，风格偏醇厚。 塔牌手工冬酿 塔牌手工冬酿是塔牌按季节生产的一条绍兴黄酒系列，由浙江塔牌绍兴酒有限公司在绍兴柯桥区湖塘酿造。它把“冬酿”写进产品名：立冬到立春投料，靠低温拉长发酵，再经压榨、煎酒、装坛陈贮。系列内部按三年、五年、六年、八年、十年分档，规格从 375 mL 到 500 mL 不等。名字描述的是季节与操作方式，不是国家标准里的等级。 塔牌手工冬酿类别配图 图：塔牌手工冬酿所属的黄酒类别配图。图片：udono，CC BY-SA 2.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是塔牌手工冬酿的产品、包装或门店实拍。 一冬一酿：立冬到立春 江南大学传统酿造食品研究中心把“冬酿”讲得很直接：从立冬到第二年立春，绍兴人在这段时间酿黄酒。理由有两条，一是气温低，杂菌难以繁殖；二是冬季鉴湖水清冽。塔牌官网的说法更细：冬至是“数九”的开始，八十一天后到惊蛰，酒醅正好发酵成熟，可以压榨、煎酒、封坛入库。两段话合起来，冬酿不是一个营销词，而是一张被气候限定的生产日历。 湖塘厂区与“纯手工”的边界 塔牌厂区在柯桥区湖塘街道，官网自述距鉴湖源头 500 米，1994 年由浙江省粮油食品进出口股份有限公司投资兴建，占地 450 亩，有 13 个黄酒酿造车间、800 余名员工，自称“全国最大纯手工酿造黄酒生产企业”；年产与单批投料量未披露。这串数字能说明产能与厂区

records.title: 必富达伦敦干金酒

records.content: 必富达伦敦干金酒 伦敦干金酒品牌，1863 年由 James Burrough 创立，在伦敦肯宁顿蒸馏；以九种植物原料蒸馏，常见酒精度 40% vol。 必富达伦敦干金酒 必富达（Beefeater）是伦敦干金酒品牌，1863 年由 James Burrough 创立，蒸馏厂位于伦敦肯宁顿（Kennington）。它以杜松子、柑橘皮、当归、甘草等约九种植物原料蒸馏，常见酒精度为 40% vol。风味以杜松子为主导，柑橘清新，辛香明显，酒体偏干。 必富达伦敦干金酒类别配图 图：必富达伦敦干金酒所属的金酒类别配图。图片：Decatur Wine & Spirits，CC BY-SA 3.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是必富达伦敦干金酒的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与身份 伦敦干金（London Dry Gin）是金酒的工艺类别，不是地理标志：它不要求必须在伦敦生产，而要求在蒸馏过程中加入植物原料，成品不得通过添加香精来制造主要风味，也不得加糖超过极低的限度。必富达是这一类别中的具体品牌，而不是“所有伦敦干金”的代名词。 金酒的核心是杜松子。不同品牌会加入柑橘皮、当归、鸢尾根、甘草、杏仁、芫荽籽等植物，形成各自的香气轮廓。必富达公开资料强调“九种植物”的配方框架，但具体比例与处理方式属于品牌信息，外界无法完整复核。理解金酒，应先看“杜松子主导 + 植物复配”的结构，再看品牌差异。 「必富达伦敦干金酒」的时间线 1863 年，James Burrough 在伦敦开始蒸馏业务，后来建立以“Beefeater”为名的品牌。品牌名与伦敦塔

records.content: 百威 美国圣路易斯安海斯-布希公司自 1876 年生产的淡色拉格，常见 5.0% vol、355 mL；以大米为辅料、在后熟罐中铺放山毛榉木条陈贮，风格清爽干净，是全球销量最大的啤酒品牌之一。 百威 1876 年，圣路易斯的德裔移民阿道夫·布希把一款淡色窖藏啤酒装进玻璃瓶，交给铁路运往全国。那时美国还没有真正意义上的“全国性啤酒品牌”：冷藏车厢与巴氏杀菌刚刚让啤酒可以跨州销售而不至于变质。百威（Budweiser）是在这个技术与市场的节点上诞生的产品，而不是先有风格定义、再有名牌。今天它的常见规格是 5.0% vol、355 mL，也是全球产量最大的啤酒品牌之一。 百威实景照片 图：百威。摄影：Budweiser bottle close-up。署名：Sam，CC BY-SA 2.0，来自 Wikimedia Commons（来源）。 一款产品，而不是一种风格 讨论百威时最容易混淆的是三个层次：安海斯-布希是生产企业，百威是品牌，瓶中的酒才是具体产品。产品由酒精度、容量、产地与批次界定；同一品牌在不同国家授权生产时，水质、原料比例与标签法规都会变化。 “美式拉格”（American lager）是一类风格：浅色、低苦度、碳酸感强、收口干净，允许使用大米或玉米等辅料。百威是这类风格最有代表性的商业产品之一，但风格名不等于产品名。称它为“美式拉格”是分类，称它为“百威”才是识别。 从移民酒馆到铁路网络 安海斯-布希的前身是埃伯哈德·安海斯在圣路易斯经营的啤酒厂。阿道夫·布希加入后，把目光放在两件当时还不寻常的事上：一是用巴氏杀菌让啤酒在运输中保持稳定，二是借助冷藏铁路车厢把啤酒卖到

records.title: 水牛足迹
records.summary: 美国肯塔基州法兰克福的肯塔基直馏波本威士忌，以玉米为主料、加入黑麦与发芽大麦，在新烧焦橡木桶中陈年；常见 45% vol、750 mL，未标注酒龄。 水牛足迹 水牛足迹是美国肯塔基州法兰克福的肯塔基直馏波本威士忌，以玉米为主料，加入黑麦与发芽大麦，在新烧焦橡木桶中陈年，常见 45% vol、750 mL。瓶身未标注酒龄
records.content: 水牛足迹 美国肯塔基州法兰克福的肯塔基直馏波本威士忌，以玉米为主料、加入黑麦与发芽大麦，在新烧焦橡木桶中陈年；常见 45% vol、750 mL，未标注酒龄。 水牛足迹 水牛足迹是美国肯塔基州法兰克福的肯塔基直馏波本威士忌，以玉米为主料，加入黑麦与发芽大麦，在新烧焦橡木桶中陈年，常见 45% vol、750 mL。瓶身未标注酒龄，属于无年份标注的常规波本。 水牛足迹相关实景照片 图：水牛足迹相关实景照片。图片：Jaimin Trivedi，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面.jpg)）。 定义与定位 先分层：威士忌是大类，波本是美国法定类型，肯塔基直馏波本是更具体的标签类别，水牛足迹是品牌与具体产品。四层分开看，才不会把产区、原料法规与品牌定位混为一谈。 “直馏”（straight）在美国法规中有明确含义：同一蒸馏季、同一蒸馏厂产出，除加水降度外不添加其他酒液或调味物质，并在新烧焦橡木桶中陈年。它不等于“单一桶”，也不等于“单一年份”，这些概念需要分开理解。 生产者与品牌 水牛足迹由水牛足迹蒸馏厂生产，酒厂位于肯塔基州法兰克福，厂址的蒸馏历史可追溯到 18 世纪末（具体年份以酒厂资料为准），现属 Sazerac 公司。酒厂同时生产多个波本与黑麦威士忌品牌。 品牌、酒厂与产品是三个层级：酒厂回答设备、原料与仓库，品牌回答定位与产品线，产品回答酒精度、容量与酒龄标注。酒厂历史属于背景信息，不能替代瓶标上的具体规格与批次。 「水牛足迹」的产地与原料 波本必须在美国境内生产，水牛足迹产自美国肯塔基州。波本的核心原料是玉米，法规要求玉米占谷物配

records.content: 杰克丹尼老7号 美国田纳西威士忌，产自林奇堡；采用林肯县木炭过滤与新烘烤橡木桶陈年，常见酒精度 40% vol。 杰克丹尼老7号 杰克丹尼老 7 号（Jack Daniel's Old No. 7）是美国田纳西威士忌，产自田纳西州林奇堡（Lynchburg）。它采用林肯县工艺（Lincoln County Process），把新蒸馏的威士忌经枫木炭过滤后再放入新烘烤橡木桶陈年，常见酒精度为 40% vol。风味以香草、焦糖、香蕉与木质香料为主。 杰克丹尼老7号 图像 图：杰克丹尼老7号。图片：Ben Jacobson ( Kranar Drogin )，CC BY 2.5，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与身份 田纳西威士忌是美国的一类威士忌，必须在美国田纳西州生产，并以枫木炭过滤（林肯县工艺）作为标识性步骤之一，再进入新烘烤橡木桶陈年。它与波本威士忌在原料与桶型上相近，但“田纳西威士忌”在标签与法规上是独立类别，不能简单等同于波本。 “老 7 号”是品牌的产品名，不是“陈年 7 年”的年份标示。杰克丹尼的标准版通常不标年龄；它的风味来自原料、木炭过滤、桶型与陈年，而不是某一个固定年份。购买时应看瓶身标签上的类别、酒精度与容量，不要从名字推断年龄。 「杰克丹尼老7号」的时间线 1866 年，Jasper Newton “Jack” Daniel 在田纳西州林奇堡登记蒸馏厂，品牌由此起步。19 世纪后期，杰克丹尼逐步建立地方市场；20 世纪则经历禁酒令、战争与行业整合。禁酒令期间，酒厂获准有限生产药用威士忌，品牌得以延续，这段历史常被品牌叙事简化。

records.content: 作品一号 作品一号是 1979 年由罗伯特·蒙大维与菲利普·德·罗斯柴尔德男爵在加州纳帕谷 Oakville 合作创立的波尔多风格干红，首个年份 1979、1984 年上市；本文从改名、四个地块、2023 年调配、Overture 与拍卖表现拆解其与 Almaviva 的差异。 作品一号 作品一号（Opus One）是美国加州纳帕谷 Oakville 的波尔多风格红葡萄酒，1979 年由罗伯特·蒙大维与菲利普·德·罗斯柴尔德男爵合作创立，首个年份 1979，1979 与 1980 两个年份在 1984 年一起上市。它以赤霞珠为主，常见 750 mL、酒精度约 14% vol。 作品一号相关实景照片 图：作品一号相关实景照片。图片：Jim G，CC BY 2.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 1979：两个家族在奥克维尔的握手 1978 年，蒙大维与罗斯柴尔德在木桐酒庄见面，很快定下合作框架：不做多个产品，只做一款酒，用纳帕的葡萄、波尔多的调配思路，由两边酿酒师共同完成。1979 年首个年份在蒙大维酒庄酿造，1984 年与 1980 年份一起上市。1989 年动工、1991 年落成自己的酒庄，建筑以石灰岩、拱廊与塔楼呼应梅多克酒庄。 从 Napa Medoc 到 Opus One：1982 年的改名 项目最初叫 “Napa Medoc”（也有资料写作 Napamedoc），把纳帕与梅多克拼在一起。1982 年改名为 Opus One：“opus”在拉丁语里是“作品”，音乐里指作曲家的第一号作品，既表示“第一款”，也表示“只做这一款”。名字的改变不只是营

records.content: 五粮液普五 五粮液核心单品的市场俗称，通常指第八代五粮液，浓香型，常见 52% vol、500 mL。本页按酒款层级说明规格、工艺与选购。 五粮液普五 “普五”是市场对五粮液核心单品的俗称，通常指第八代五粮液。它属于浓香型白酒，常见规格为 52% vol、500 mL，产自四川宜宾。理解这一酒款，需要同时看品牌、生产者与具体规格，而不是只看“五粮液”三个字。 五粮液普五类别配图 图：五粮液普五所属的白酒类别配图。图片：Xiaomage de，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是五粮液普五的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 “普五”不是官方品名，而是消费者与渠道对核心单品的简称，用来区别于 1618、系列酒与纪念版。它属于白酒中的浓香型路线，定位是品牌的核心产品，而不是入门款或限量款。 同一品牌下还有低度版本与不同包装版本。度数、容量、包装与批次都会影响体验与价格，因此“普五”三个字不足以确定一瓶酒的全部信息，最终仍要回到标签。 生产者与品牌 酒款由集团体系生产，品牌由五粮液承载，生产与销售由上市平台承担。集团、上市公司、品牌、产品是四个层级，数据口径与责任主体不同。 因此，看到“普五出厂价”“普五批价”一类说法时，要先确认是官方指导价、渠道成交价还是某一年的市场报价。价格信息时效性强，本页不给出具体数字，只说明口径差异。 「五粮液普五」的产地与原料 宜宾位于四川南部，岷江与金沙江汇合后进入长江，河谷气候湿润，适合开放式制曲与长期窖池发酵。放到中国白酒产区的格局里，宜宾是浓香型的重要节点。 原料为高粱、大米

records.content: 习酒·窖藏1988 贵州习酒的核心酱香型单品，常见规格为 53% vol、500 mL，定位次高端；产品名中的 1988 指向企业当年的获奖节点，正式品名与规格仍以标签为准。 习酒·窖藏1988 习酒·窖藏1988 是贵州习酒的核心酱香型单品，常见规格为 53% vol、500 mL，产自贵州习水县习酒镇。它属于白酒中的酱香路线，市场定位在次高端。产品名中的“1988”指向企业当年的获奖节点，但名称不等于酒龄，也不等于瓶中所装基酒的年份。 习酒·窖藏1988类别配图 图：习酒·窖藏1988所属的白酒类别配图。图片：Xiaomage de，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是习酒·窖藏1988的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 “习酒·窖藏1988”是正式品名，不是对某一年份酒液的描述。它由贵州习酒生产，由习酒品牌承载，产品线内部还有不同版本与包装。讨论价格与品质时，应先把“品牌”“单品”“版本”“批次”分开。 这款产品处在次高端价格带，是习酒流通面较广的核心单品。它既不是入门款，也不是限量纪念款；同一品名下可能出现雅致版、精装版等不同包装版本，酒体与规格是否相同，应以当期标签和企业说明为准，不能只凭外观判断。 生产者与品牌 生产主体是贵州习酒股份有限公司，位于贵州遵义市习水县习酒镇。企业前身可追溯到明代万历年间的殷姓白酒作坊，1952 年通过收购组建为国营企业，1998 年加入茅台集团，2022 年整体变更设立股份有限公司。股份公司、控股集团、品牌与单品是不同层级，责任主体与数据口径也不同。 品牌层面，“

records.content: 迎驾洞藏16 安徽迎驾贡酒洞藏系列的代表产品，浓香型白酒，常见 52% vol 或 42% vol、500 mL；以多粮原料与黄岩洞、清潭洞贮存为公开特点。 迎驾洞藏16 “迎驾洞藏16”是迎驾贡酒洞藏系列中的一款浓香型产品，常见规格为 52% vol 或 42% vol、500 mL，产自安徽霍山。它把多粮浓香、长周期发酵与山洞贮存放在同一个产品叙事里，名称中的“16”是系列编号，不能直接当作瓶中酒龄。 迎驾洞藏16类别配图 图：迎驾洞藏16所属的白酒类别配图。图片：Xiaomage de，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是迎驾洞藏16的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 洞藏系列在迎驾的产品结构中承担次高端与商务宴请，和大众价位的迎驾贡酒主系列、礼赠导向的大师版形成分层。理解这款酒，要同时看品牌、生产者、具体规格与贮存方式，而不是只看“洞藏”两个字。 “洞藏16”是产品名，不是质量等级，也不是年份证明。企业公开资料中的“生态洞藏”描述的是贮存环境与产品线名称，消费者仍应回到瓶身标签核对酒精度、容量、原料与生产商。 生产者与品牌 酒款由安徽迎驾贡酒股份有限公司组织生产，品牌由迎驾贡酒承载。该公司于 2003 年 11 月 28 日成立，注册地在安徽省霍山县佛子岭镇，2015 年 5 月 28 日在上海证券交易所上市。 集团、股份公司、品牌与产品是四个层级：品牌回答“叫什么、面向谁”，股份公司回答“谁持有商标、谁承担法律责任”，产品则回答具体度数、容量与批次。把“生态酿酒”直接当作质量认证，是把企业定位与

records.title: 敖云
records.summary: 云南迪庆香格里拉高海拔产区出产的赤霞珠干红，由酩悦·轩尼诗-路易·威登集团投资建设；首个年份为 2013，常见 750 mL、酒精度约 13%-14% vol，具体年份与批次以瓶标为准。 敖云 敖云（Ao Yun）是云南迪庆香格里拉高海拔产区出产的赤霞珠干红，由酩悦·轩尼诗-路易·威登集团投资建设，首个年份为 2013
records.content: 敖云 云南迪庆香格里拉高海拔产区出产的赤霞珠干红，由酩悦·轩尼诗-路易·威登集团投资建设；首个年份为 2013，常见 750 mL、酒精度约 13%-14% vol，具体年份与批次以瓶标为准。 敖云 敖云（Ao Yun）是云南迪庆香格里拉高海拔产区出产的赤霞珠干红，由酩悦·轩尼诗-路易·威登集团投资建设，首个年份为 2013。酒款属于红葡萄酒，常见 750 mL 瓶装、酒精度约 13%-14% vol，具体年份、装瓶批次与酒标信息以瓶标为准。 敖云 图像 图：敖云。图片：Charlie fong，Public domain，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。 定义与定位 敖云是一个具体的葡萄酒产品，也是一个由中国高海拔产区生产的国际品牌。它在葡萄酒的分类里属于静态红葡萄酒，不是加强酒，也不是起泡酒。产品名与产区名不是同一件事：敖云回答“哪一款酒”，香格里拉回答“在哪种”。 这个项目的定位是高端干红：以赤霞珠为主体，在海拔较高的地块种植与酿造，再用橡木桶陈酿。高端定位来自产区条件与工艺投入，而不是来自名称本身；判断具体酒款仍要看年份、批次与瓶标。 产区与气候 产区位于云南西北部迪庆藏族自治州香格里拉一带，葡萄园分布在海拔约 2,200 米以上的河谷坡地。高海拔带来强烈的日照、较大的昼夜温差与较长的成熟期，葡萄在白天积累糖分与风味，夜间低温则有助于保留酸度。 这里的气候受季风影响，雨季与采收期可能重叠，霜冻、冰雹与降雨都是风险。不同海拔、坡向与土壤的地块成熟节奏不同，酒庄需要分批采收与筛选。高海拔不是质量保证，它只是改变了成熟与酸度的平衡条件。 品种与栽培 敖

records.title: 古越龙山花雕酒
records.summary: 浙江绍兴黄酒品牌，以糯米、麦曲和鉴湖水酿造，花雕、加饭等产品常见酒精度 15%–18% vol。 古越龙山花雕酒 古越龙山是浙江绍兴的黄酒品牌，主打花雕、加饭等绍兴酒产品。它以糯米、麦曲和鉴湖水酿造，经压榨、煎酒和陈酿，酒精度通常在 15%–18% vol。 古越龙山花雕酒类别配图 古越龙山花雕酒所属的黄酒类别配图。图
records.content: 古越龙山花雕酒 浙江绍兴黄酒品牌，以糯米、麦曲和鉴湖水酿造，花雕、加饭等产品常见酒精度 15%–18% vol。 古越龙山花雕酒 古越龙山是浙江绍兴的黄酒品牌，主打花雕、加饭等绍兴酒产品。它以糯米、麦曲和鉴湖水酿造，经压榨、煎酒和陈酿，酒精度通常在 15%–18% vol。 古越龙山花雕酒类别配图 图：古越龙山花雕酒所属的黄酒类别配图。图片：udono，CC BY-SA 2.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面）。这张图片用于标识品类，不是古越龙山花雕酒的产品、包装或门店实拍。 定义与定位 古越龙山是企业与品牌名称，产品属于黄酒中的绍兴酒类型。绍兴酒是地理标志产品，对产地范围、原料与工艺有明确要求；品牌则是在这一产区传统之上形成的具体产品体系。 需要区分三个层级：黄酒是大类，绍兴酒是产区与传统工艺，古越龙山是品牌。三者不能互相替代。花雕、加饭、善酿、香雪是绍兴酒中的产品称谓，指向不同的配料比例与糖分风格，而不是四个互相独立的酒种。 产区与环境 绍兴位于浙江北部、钱塘江南岸，属亚热带季风气候，四季分明、湿润多雨。鉴湖水系是绍兴酒酿造的重要水源，水体与当地气候共同影响发酵与酒体风格。传统上重视冬季酿造，低温有利于控制发酵速度与杂菌。 产区条件不只是一种叙事。水质、气温、空气微生物与稻米供应，都会落到具体的发酵结果上。地理标志的意义在于把这些条件与工艺要求固定下来，但同一产区内不同企业、不同批次仍有差异，仍需以标签与产品信息为准。 原料与制曲 主料是糯米，要求颗粒饱满、淀粉含量高。曲以小麦制成的麦曲为主，承担糖化与部分香气形成。制曲的温度与时间影响酶活力与微生物组

records.title: 竹叶青酒
records.summary: 以汾酒为基酒，加入竹叶与多种植物配料、糖等配制而成的露酒，常见酒精度约 38% vol，产自山西汾阳杏花村；风味清甜，带草本香气。 竹叶青酒 竹叶青酒是以汾酒为基酒，加入竹叶与多种植物配料、糖等配制而成的露酒，常见酒精度约 38% vol，产自山西汾阳杏花村。它风味清甜，带草本香气，是配制酒中认知度较高的一款。 竹叶青
records.content: 竹叶青酒 以汾酒为基酒，加入竹叶与多种植物配料、糖等配制而成的露酒，常见酒精度约 38% vol，产自山西汾阳杏花村；风味清甜，带草本香气。 竹叶青酒 竹叶青酒是以汾酒为基酒，加入竹叶与多种植物配料、糖等配制而成的露酒，常见酒精度约 38% vol，产自山西汾阳杏花村。它风味清甜，带草本香气，是配制酒中认知度较高的一款。 竹叶青酒 图像 图：竹叶青酒。图片：N509FZ，CC BY-SA 4.0，via Wikimedia Commons（原图页面.jpg)）。 定义与定位 这款酒属于配制酒（露酒），由山西杏花村汾酒厂股份有限公司生产，品牌由汾酒承载。它在产品结构中承担“低度、易饮、带草本风味”的位置，与清香型白酒的定位不同。 需要区分三个层级：白酒是基酒类别，配制酒是成品类别，竹叶青是具体产品。基酒用的是汾酒，但成品不是单纯的白酒，不能按清香型白酒的品评标准去要求它。 生产者与品牌 酒款由山西杏花村汾酒厂股份有限公司组织生产，品牌由汾酒承载。产区在山西汾阳杏花村，属于中国清香型白酒的核心产区之一。 公司、品牌与产品是三个层级：品牌回答“叫什么、面向谁”，公司回答“谁持有商标、谁承担法律责任”，产品则回答具体配料、酒精度与容量。把基酒的产区与工艺直接套到成品上，是常见的层级混淆。 「竹叶青酒」的产地与原料 杏花村位于山西汾阳，属温带大陆性季风气候，四季分明、昼夜温差较大。当地的水源与微生物环境是清香型白酒酿造的重要条件。 基酒以高粱等粮谷为原料，经固态发酵与蒸馏取得。成品的配料还包括竹叶与多种植物配料、糖等，具体名单与比例属于企业配方，标签通常只披露部分信息，购买时应以瓶标为准

Kouzijiao Kouzijiao belongs to a very specific setting: the old town of Suixi on the Huaibei plain, where rivers and roads meet and where distillery workshops once lined the streets. The place gave the brand the word "kouzi", a local term for a junction or opening, while "jiao" refers to the fermentation pit. Together they point to origin and to pit fermentation at once. records.content: Shede A high-end strong-aroma baijiu brand under Shede Spirits, launched in December 2001; positioned around the Shede cultural idea and aged-liquor reserves, with Pinwei Shede, Zhihui Shede, collectible Shede and crystal Shede in the range. Shede Shede is a case of turning a philosophical phrase into a baijiu brand. "Shede" is an everyday expression meaning to give something up in order to gain something, and in 2001 the company registered it as a high-end strong-aroma brand. The idea was to give up part of short-term scale in exchange for aged-liquor reserves and brand premium. The brand belongs to Shede Spirits Co., Ltd. and is made in Tuopai, Shehong, Sichuan. records.content: Aviation Recorded in 1916 by Hugo Ensslin of New York's Hotel Wallick in Recipes for Mixed Drinks, the Aviation combines gin, maraschino, lemon juice and crème de violette; it is pale violet to grey-blue and usually garnished with a cherry. Aviation The Aviation is one of the few cocktails whose colour is itself evidence of the recipe. Its pale violet comes from crème de violette, not from syrup or food dye; when that liqueur disappeared from the market, the drink quietly became something else. Boulevardier The Boulevardier is a classic cocktail of whiskey, Campari and sweet vermouth. It is often described as a whiskey Negroni, but the two drinks do not share an identical ratio history. The Boulevardier as recorded in 1927 is usually retold as equal parts of all three ingredients. The IBA's current formula is 45 ml whiskey, 30 ml Campari and 30 ml sweet vermouth, roughly 1.5:1:1. records.content: Martinez A classic of gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino and orange bitters, dating to the 1880s in the United States. It bridges the Manhattan and the dry martini, with a delicate bitter-sweet balance. Martinez The Martinez combines gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino and orange bitters. It is often described as a gin Manhattan and as an ancestor of the dry martini: the same gin-and-vermouth spine, but with the sweetness of cherry liqueur and the orange scent of bitters, giving a rounder, softer drink. Mimosa The mimosa is the most familiar sparkling-wine cocktail on a brunch table: equal parts champagne and orange juice, poured into a flute, sometimes finished with a strip of orange peel. Low in alcohol, fine in bubbles and the colour of morning light, it is easier to like than most classics. Simple does not mean careless. Moscow Mule The Moscow Mule is a long drink built from vodka, ginger beer and fresh lime. It became popular in 1970s California and reached a wide audience through a rock band's tour. Tequila Sunrise The Tequila Sunrise looks more complicated than it drinks. Tequila, orange juice and grenadine form a gradient from orange-yellow to deep red in a highball, like the sky at dawn. The recipe is short, but the layering and the balance need a little order and patience. The drink became popular in California in the 1970s and later reached a wide audience through a rock band's tour and bar culture. Its name, colour and pop history matter almost as much as its taste. records.content: Tom Collins A long drink of Old Tom gin, lemon juice, syrup and soda water; the IBA lists it under John Collins (45 ml gin, 30 ml lemon juice, 15 ml syrup, 60 ml soda), notes Old Tom for a true Tom Collins, and serves it over ice in a Collins glass with lemon and cherry. records.content: Vieux Carré A New Orleans classic of rye whiskey, Cognac, sweet vermouth, Bénédictine and two bitters, defined by its double base and herbal sweetness. Vieux Carré The Vieux Carré is a short drink of rye whiskey, Cognac, sweet vermouth, Bénédictine and Peychaud's and Angostura bitters. It is usually stirred, strained over ice into a rocks glass and garnished with an orange twist and a cocktail cherry. Rye brings spice, Cognac brings fruit, sweet vermouth brings herbal sweetness, Bénédictine adds honey and spice, and the two bitters give the drink its aromatic top and its long, dry finish. records.content: Zombie A tiki classic created by Donn Beach in Hollywood in 1934, built on Jamaican, Puerto Rican and Demerara rums with falernum, Donn's Mix and grenadine; strong and usually garnished with a mint sprig. Zombie The Zombie is not "a tropical drink with a lot of rum in it." It is the signature cocktail that Don the Beachcomber built in Hollywood in 1934 and deliberately kept out of rivals' reach: the recipe was written in code, and even the bartenders did not know what was in the bottles. What allows us to make it today is the later detective work on an old notebook and a set of syrup code names. Zombie photograph Figure: Zombie. Photograph: Zombie cocktail gianni zottola. records.content: Agave Agave is a succulent genus whose heart, or piña, is rich in inulin-type fructans; after cooking and hydrolysis it is fermented and distilled into tequila and mezcal, with species, maturity and roasting method shaping flavour. Agave Agave is a genus of perennial succulents native to the Americas, with more than two hundred species. Distillers do not use the leaves but the heart, or piña, formed by the swollen stem and leaf bases. That tissue stores fructans rather than starch, so sugar release depends on cooking or roasting rather than malt enzymes. Much of the difference between tequila and mezcal begins here.Agave image Figure: Agave. Image: Marc Ryckaert ( MJJR ), CC BY-SA 3.0, via W

Apple The apple (Malus domestica) is the fruit of a deciduous tree in the rose family. Dessert apples are bred for sweetness, crispness and juice; cider apples are bred for acidity, tannin and aroma, which are almost opposite goals. records.content: Barley An annual cereal of the genus Hordeum; after malting it becomes the base material for beer and whisky, and in baijiu daqu it is often paired with wheat and peas. Barley Barley is an annual cereal of the genus Hordeum in the grass family, with the cultivated species usually written Hordeum vulgare. It tolerates cold and adapts widely, serving as food and feed as well as the base material for beer and whisky. Its most important processed form is malt: after the grain germinates, starch enzymes are produced that break starch into fermentable sugar, and this step determines the saccharifying capacity of beer and whisky.Barley image Figure: Barley. records.content: Buckwheat Buckwheat is a pseudocereal in the Polygonaceae family and contains no gluten; it is used in buckwheat beer, soba shochu and some regional baijiu, bringing earthy, honeyed and grainy notes, while its protein and starch require separate adjustments in saccharification and fermentation. Buckwheat Buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum) belongs to the Polygonaceae family. Its seed is a triangular achene rather than a true cereal grain, which is why it is classed as a pseudocereal. It contains no gluten of the kind found in wheat or barley, yet it brings starch, protein and flavonoids such as rutin into a fermentation. records.content: Glutinous rice A rice type whose starch is almost entirely amylopectin, becoming very sticky and soft after cooking; it is a typical raw material for yellow wine and some sweet rice drinks, and often appears in multi-grain baijiu recipes. Glutinous rice Glutinous rice is a type of rice that is extremely sticky because its starch is almost entirely amylopectin. In Chinese it is also called jiangmi, and in brewing it is often called wine rice. Steamed glutinous rice is soft and clumps together; it is used for foods such as rice dumplings and eight-treasure rice, and is also an important component of yellow wine, sweet rice drinks and multi-grain baijiu. records.content: Grape The fruit of Vitis vines; wine grapes are selected for sugar, acid, pigment and tannin balance, unlike table grapes bred for eating. Grape The grape is the fruit of a vine in the genus Vitis. The European grape used for winemaking (Vitis vinifera) and the table grape sold in supermarkets are not bred for the same goals: wine grapes are valued for sugar-acid balance, pigment, tannin and aroma precursors, while table grapes are valued for berry size, texture and keeping quality. The OIV definition of wine requires it to come entirely from the fermentation of fresh grapes or grape juice, which shows that the grape is both a raw material and part of the boundary of the wine category. records.content: Honey Honey is the sweet substance bees make from nectar, dominated by glucose and fructose; it is the sole sugar source of mead and can add aroma to beer, liqueurs and spirits, but low nitrogen, high sugar and low pH make fermentation hard to start. Honey Honey is the sweet substance bees make from nectar through their own enzymes and evaporation. Its sugars are mainly fructose and glucose, moisture is usually below 20%, and it carries small amounts of organic acids, enzymes, minerals and pollen. As the sole sugar source of mead, the difficulty is not sweetness but the sluggish fermentation caused by low nitrogen, high sugar and low pH together.Honey image Figure: Honey. Image: Scott Bauer,

records.content: Hops Hops are the female flower cones of a perennial climbing plant in the Cannabaceae family; alpha acids isomerise during the boil to give bitterness, essential oils give aroma, and polyphenols and antibacterial compounds affect foam, clarity and shelf life. Hops Hops (Humulus lupulus) are a perennial climbing plant in the Cannabaceae family. Brewing uses the unpollinated female cones, which supply bitterness, aroma, antibacterial protection and foam stability. Bitterness does not come directly from alpha acids: it appears when alpha acids isomerise into iso-alpha acids during the boil. Aroma comes from essential oils, and the two want opposite timing. records.content: Maize An annual cereal of the genus Zea with high starch content and fat concentrated in the germ; it is a common ingredient in multi-grain baijiu and a core raw material in American bourbon and some beer adjuncts. Maize Maize is an annual cereal of the genus Zea in the grass family, native to the Americas and now grown worldwide. Its starch content is high and its fat is concentrated in the germ; it is used as food and feed, and as a raw material for multi-grain baijiu, bourbon whisky and some beers. records.content: Millet Millet is the hulled grain of foxtail millet (Setaria italica) and a general name for small-seeded cereals such as proso and pearl millet; in China it is used in huangjiu and millet wine, and in Africa and Asia for traditional cloudy grain beers, with starch and protein shaping saccharification and flavour. Millet Millet is the hulled grain of foxtail millet (Setaria italica), about 1–2 mm across and ranging from pale yellow to orange-red. Northern China has a long history of growing it, and it appears in huangjiu, millet wine and some regional baijiu. records.content: Molasses Molasses is the syrup left after sugar crystallisation, containing sucrose, glucose, fructose and minerals; it is the main sugar source for rum and a common industrial yeast medium, and its grade and composition shape fermentation speed and flavour. Molasses Molasses is the thick syrup left after sugar crystals are separated from cane or beet juice. It carries sucrose, invert sugar, minerals and nitrogenous matter into the fermenter, and it is the main sugar source for rum. The old label of "waste molasses" is misleading: grade, ash content and microbial load directly change fermentation speed, distillation yield and body.Molasses image Figure: Molasses. records.content: Oats Oats are an annual cereal of the genus Avena with high fat and beta-glucan content; they bring silky body and haze to beer and are traditional in oatmeal stout, but fat and viscosity make saccharification, lautering and distillation harder than with barley. Oats Oats (Avena sativa) are an annual cereal of the genus Avena that prefers cool, moist climates. Their fat and beta-glucan levels are clearly higher than barley. In beer they mostly supply body, creaminess and haze rather than sugar; in oatmeal stout that silky texture has become a style marker. records.title: Rice

records.content: Rice The grain left after rice is husked and milled, and an important starch source for baijiu, yellow wine and sake; japonica and indica rice differ in starch structure, stickiness and steaming behaviour, which directly affect saccharification and fermentation. Rice Rice is the grain left after paddy is husked and milled, and belongs to the genus Oryza in the grass family. It is a staple across Asia and an important starch source for baijiu, yellow wine and sake. Unlike wheat and sorghum, rice has less protein and fat, its starch granules are fine, and it becomes sticky after cooking; these traits shape how it behaves in saccharification and fermentation. records.content: Rye Rye is an annual cereal of the genus Secale, hardy and tolerant of poor soil; it is the required base of American rye whiskey and brings a spicy, dry grain character to beer, while beta-glucans and proteins make saccharification and lautering harder. Rye Rye (Secale cereale) is an annual or biennial cereal of the genus Secale, hardy and tolerant of poor soil, able to grow at latitudes where wheat struggles to overwinter. It is the required base of American rye whiskey, the flour behind German and Nordic rye bread, and in beer a spicy, dry grain backbone. records.content: Sorghum An annual cereal of the genus Sorghum and one of the main grain ingredients in Chinese baijiu; the balance of starch, protein, fat and tannin in the grain shapes fermentation and flavour. Sorghum Sorghum is an annual herb of the genus Sorghum in the grass family, with the cultivated species usually written Sorghum bicolor. FAO material lists it as an important cereal in the dry and semi-arid regions of Africa and Asia, with names including great millet and kaoliang; in China it is also often called shushu or hongliang. It tolerates drought and heat and is highly adaptable, serving as food and feed as well as an important raw material for baijiu, yellow wine and vinegar.Sorghum image

records.content: Sugarcane Sugarcane is a tall grass of the genus Saccharum whose stems store sucrose; pressing the juice and fermenting it directly yields cane-juice rum and Brazilian cane spirit, while refining sugar first and fermenting the molasses gives the other major rum route. Sugarcane Sugarcane is a perennial C4 grass of the genus Saccharum whose stem works like a sugar pipeline, storing photosynthate as sucrose at 12–16%. It underpins the global sugar industry and is the starting point for rum, cachaça and agricultural rum. records.content: Water The most easily overlooked yet ubiquitous ingredient in brewing; its minerals, hardness and pH affect saccharification, fermentation, microbial activity and final flavour, and have long shaped where distilleries and breweries are sited. Water Water is the most easily overlooked ingredient in brewing. It makes up most of the volume of the finished drink and takes part in saccharification, fermentation, distillation and dilution, and it also affects microbial activity and equipment cleaning. Different drinks have different water requirements: beer focuses on mineral ions and saccharification pH, whisky on water source and tradition, baijiu on water added for dilution, and sake is highly

records.title: Wheat
records.summary: An annual cereal of the genus Triticum, used as a staple food and as a key ingredient in qu making, multi-grain baijiu, beer and whisky; the balance of protein
records.content: Wheat An annual cereal of the genus Triticum, used as a staple food and as a key ingredient in qu making, multi-grain baijiu, beer and whisky; the balance of protein and starch shapes both qu quality and the body of the drink. Wheat Wheat is an annual cereal of the genus Triticum in the grass family, with common wheat, Triticum aestivum, dominating cultivation. It is both a global staple and a brewing raw material: qu making, multi-grain baijiu, beer and whisky may all use wheat or wheat products. Compared with sorghum and rice, wheat contains more protein and gluten, which gives it a different role in qu making and fermentation than a pure starch source. Wheat image Figure: Wheat. Image: ka

records.title: Yeast
records.summary: is a single-celled fungus that turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide and produces esters, higher alcohols and other flavour compounds; strain, pitching me
records.content: Yeast Yeast is a single-celled fungus that turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide and produces esters, higher alcohols and other flavour compounds; strain, pitching method and temperature steer fermentation, making yeast the most important and most overlooked variable in brewing. Yeast Yeast is a single-celled fungus that turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide during fermentation, and it shapes flavour through esters, higher alcohols, glycerol and organic acids. It both executes fermentation and creates style. Change the strain or the temperature on the same wort or juice and the result can be entirely different, which is why yeast is often called the most overlooked ingredient.Yea

records.title: Blending
records.summary: Combining liquids from different batches, vintages, varieties or cask types in set proportions to stabilise quality, balance structure or build a fixed style; w
records.content: Blending Combining liquids from different batches, vintages, varieties or cask types in set proportions to stabilise quality, balance structure or build a fixed style; wine, Champagne, whisky, brandy and baijiu follow different rules and logics. Blending Blending is the process of combining liquids from different batches, vintages, varieties, regions or cask types in set proportions. It can be a technical tool for consistency or the core of style design. Wine, Champagne, whisky, brandy and baijiu all blend, but the permitted scope, terminology and goals differ. Reading blending as simply "mixing things together" ignores proportional design, sensory calibration and the settling that follows.

records.content: Distillation A process that separates and concentrates ethanol from a fermented liquid or mash by exploiting differences in boiling points; equipment, reflux and cut points shape the spirit's flavour. Distillation Distillation separates ethanol from water and other volatile components by exploiting differences in boiling points. Fermented liquid or mash usually contains only a low concentration of ethanol; heating, vaporisation and condensation produce a distillate with higher alcohol strength. Distillation is essential to brandy, whisky, rum, vodka and baijiu, but different drinks choose equipment and cut points very differently.Whisky flow: malting, mashing, fermentation, distillation, oak

records.content: Fermentation The metabolic process in which yeast or bacteria convert sugar into ethanol, carbon dioxide and flavour compounds under low oxygen; strain, temperature, sugar concentration, pH and oxygen set speed, strength and aroma. Fermentation Fermentation is the metabolic process in which yeast or bacteria break down sugar under low-oxygen conditions and produce ethanol, carbon dioxide and flavour compounds. It converts the chemical energy of sugar into cellular energy and releases ethanol as a waste product. records.title: Fortification
records.summary: The addition of grape spirit to wine to raise alcohol and stabilise the wine; fortifying mid-fermentation retains residual sugar, while fortifying after ferment
records.content: Fortification The addition of grape spirit to wine to raise alcohol and stabilise the wine; fortifying mid-fermentation retains residual sugar, while fortifying after fermentation gives a dry fortified style, so timing and proportion decide the result. Fortification Fortification is the addition of distilled spirit to wine. The spirit is usually grape-derived alcohol or brandy, and the aim is to raise the alcohol of the finished wine, suppress microbial activity, stabilise the wine and, in the process, retain sugar or shape flavour. Fortified wine is a category of its own precisely because this step rewrites where fermentation ends, rather than merely raising an alcohol number. Fortification

records.content: Kimoto and yamahai Two traditional sake-mother routes that rely on natural lactic acid bacteria; kimoto keeps the yamafuri mashing step while yamahai omits it, and both differ from the sokujo route that adds lactic acid, shaping acidity, umami and production time. Kimoto and yamahai Kimoto and yamahai are two traditional sake-mother methods for sake, both relying on natural lactic acid bacteria to acidify the mother instead of adding lactic acid. Kimoto keeps the yamafuri step, in which the mixture is mashed into a paste, while yamahai omits it. records.content: Lagering The cold-storage stage after primary fermentation, in which yeast takes up diacetyl, suspended solids settle, sulfur compounds disperse and natural carbonation settles; the temperature curve, time and dissolved oxygen decide the cleanliness and shelf life of lager. Lagering Lagering sits after primary fermentation and before filtration and filling. The German verb lagern means "to store", and the stage places the beer in conditions close to freezing so that yeast metabolism, colloidal settling and carbonation can finish slowly. records.title: Lees ageing
records.summary: An ageing method that keeps wine in contact with the fine lees left after fermentation; stirring frequency, temperature and time bring roundness, creamy and bre
records.content: Lees ageing An ageing method that keeps wine in contact with the fine lees left after fermentation; stirring frequency, temperature and time bring roundness, creamy and bready notes and a reductive barrier, but poor handling produces sulfides and bitterness. Lees ageing Lees ageing (French sur lie) keeps wine in contact with the lees that settle after fermentation. The bulk of the lees is spent yeast, mixed with a little grape debris and tartrate. Gross lees are coarse and prone to spoilage and are usually separated quickly; fine lees are small, slow to settle and may deliberately be retained. records.title: Malolactic fermentation
records.summary: A secondary fermentation in which lactic acid bacteria convert malic acid into lactic acid and carbon dioxide; it lowers titratable acidity, raises pH and softe
records.content: Malolactic fermentation A secondary fermentation in which lactic acid bacteria convert malic acid into lactic acid and carbon dioxide; it lowers titratable acidity, raises pH and softens texture, adding creamy notes in moderation but volatile acidity, biogenic amines and haze when uncontrolled. Malolactic fermentation Malolactic fermentation, shortened to MLF, is a secondary fermentation in wine. It is often confused with alcoholic fermentation, but the agents differ completely: alcoholic fermentation uses yeast to turn sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide, while malolactic fermentation uses lactic acid bacteria to turn malic acid into lactic acid and carbon dioxide and produces no alcohol.

records.title: Malting
records.summary: The pre-treatment that steeps, germinates, kilns and de-roots barley and other grains; the degree of germination and the kilning curve set amylase power, modifi
records.content: Malting The pre-treatment that steeps, germinates, kilns and de-roots barley and other grains; the degree of germination and the kilning curve set amylase power, modification and colour, and therefore saccharification efficiency and finished flavour. Malting Malting turns barley and other grains into malt. Its core is not simply letting grain sprout: germination wakes the grain's own enzyme system, and kilning then fixes those enzymes and drives moisture down. Beer and whisky both depend on malting, because without the amylases supplied by malt, saccharification cannot convert endosperm starch into fermentable sugar. Malting image Figure: Malting. records.title: Mixed steaming and distillation

records.content: Mixed steaming and distillation A solid-state baijiu arrangement in which fresh grain and fermented mash are steamed in the same vessel and spirit is collected in one pass, as opposed to separate steaming; it usually works with continuous mash replenishment and shapes grain aroma, body and pit cycling. Mixed steaming and distillation Mixed steaming and distillation is how solid-state baijiu organises distillation: freshly mixed grain powder, filler and the mash waiting to be distilled are loaded into the same steamer, so grain cooking and spirit distillation happen in one pass and grain aromas enter the condenser with the spirit. records.summary: Storing wine or spirit in oak casks so that wood, trace oxygen and time change aroma, tannin, colour and texture; species, cask size, age and toast level are ad
records.content: Oak ageing Storing wine or spirit in oak casks so that wood, trace oxygen and time change aroma, tannin, colour and texture; species, cask size, age and toast level are adjustable variables. Oak ageing Oak ageing means storing wine or spirit in oak casks for a period so that wood, oxygen and time change the drink together. It is not simply "putting it in a barrel" but a set of adjustable variables: oak species, cask size, age, toast level, ageing environment and duration all affect the final style. records.content: Pressing Pressing separates juice or wine from skins, seeds and stems. White wines are usually pressed before fermentation, red wines after maceration or fermentation, and the pressure curve and fraction cuts decide yield, tannin and body. Pressing Pressing separates juice or wine from skins, seeds and stems. It looks like simple squeezing, but it is a trade-off over pressure, time and fraction cuts: more pressure raises yield but also pulls in tannin, colour and bitterness; less pressure gives cleaner liquid but lower volume. records.title: Qu making
records.summary: A traditional process that cultures moulds, yeasts and bacteria on grain to make a saccharifying and fermenting starter; qu quality and microbial community dire
records.content: Qu making A traditional process that cultures moulds, yeasts and bacteria on grain to make a saccharifying and fermenting starter; qu quality and microbial community directly affect yield and flavour in baijiu and yellow wine. Qu making Qu making is a key step in traditional Chinese brewing: culturing microbes on grain to make a saccharifying and fermenting starter. Qu is not a single yeast but a carrier on which moulds, yeasts and bacteria grow together; it both breaks starch down into sugar and takes part in fermentation and aroma production. Baijiu, yellow wine and some other grain drinks depend on qu, but the qu types and processes differ. Qu making image Figure: Qu making. Image: Uranas

records.summary: The process that breaks starch in grains and other raw materials into fermentable sugars; malt enzymes, mould enzymes from qu, temperature, pH and the water-to-
records.content: Saccharification The process that breaks starch in grains and other raw materials into fermentable sugars; malt enzymes, mould enzymes from qu, temperature, pH and the water-to-grain ratio set the sugar profile and shape body, yield and fermentation. Saccharification Saccharification breaks grain starch into sugars that yeast can use. Starch is a polymer of glucose, and its granules are wrapped in protein and lipid, so pitching yeast directly onto grain ferments almost nothing. Only after gelatinisation and enzymatic hydrolysis into glucose, maltose and maltotriose can the sugar enter fermentation. records.content: Solid-state fermentation Fermentation carried out on a low-moisture solid grain mash, the basis of solid-state baijiu; unlike semi-solid and liquid routes, vessels, qu and temperature management shape the flavour. Solid-state fermentation Solid-state fermentation is a form of fermentation used in baijiu: the substrate has a low moisture content, the grain mash stays solid, and microorganisms grow in a loose matrix of grain particles, qu powder and filler. Kimmeridgian limestone and marl rich in marine fossils, a cool climate and Chardonnay alone define it, across four tiers from Petit Chablis to Grand Cru, the latter with only 7 climats. Chablis Chablis is the northernmost white-wine region of Burgundy, in the Serein valley of the Yonne, with about 5800 ha of vines. It makes white wine from Chardonnay alone and is known for high acidity and a mineral character in a cool climate. records.content: Champagne A sparkling wine appellation in northern France, centred on Reims and Épernay, with vineyards in the Montagne de Reims, the Vallée de la Marne, the Côte des Blancs and the Côte des Bar to the south. It is made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier by the traditional method of in-bottle second fermentation, aged on the lees and labelled by sweetness level. Champagne Champagne is the sparkling wine appellation of the Champagne region in northern France and the only legal home of the protected name Champagne. records.content: Châteauneuf-du-Pape An appellation in the Southern Rhône north of Avignon, granted AOC status in 1936. Galets roulés on the La Crau plateau, the mistral and Grenache-led blends form its backbone; the permitted list is commonly summarised as 13 varieties, but it is a permitted range rather than a fixed recipe. Châteauneuf-du-Pape Châteauneuf-du-Pape is an appellation in the Southern Rhône, north of Avignon, with vineyards spread across the plateaus and hills of the Rhône's left bank. Its first impression is often "full-bodied, spicy, high in alcohol", but what really shapes the style is the heat of the stone-covered plateaus, the drying mistral and a blending tradition built on Grenache. records.content: Cognac A grape brandy region in the Charente area of France, built on Ugni Blanc, double pot distillation and French oak ageing, with VS, VSOP and XO grades defined by minimum age. Cognac Cognac is a grape brandy region in western France, in the Charente area, and the name of the grape brandy made around it. It is based mainly on Ugni Blanc, distilled twice in pot stills, then aged in French oak to produce the VS, VSOP and XO grades defined by minimum age. Cognac image Figure: Cognac. records.content: Colchagua Wine zone within the Rapel sub-region of Chile's Central Valley, covering Colchagua and Cardenal Caro provinces. On Wines of Chile's variety figures the main varieties total about 28,600 hectares, led by Cabernet Sauvignon at 11,928, Carmenère at 3,657 and Merlot at 3,132. A Mediterranean climate, warm and dry inland and cooler near the Pacific in the west. Soils are alluvial terraces, Andean foothill deposits and coastal granitic hills. Legal areas include San Fernando, Chimbarongo, Nancagua and Santa Cruz, and Reserva is not a quality grade. records.content: Columbia Valley AVA covering central and south-central Washington, south-eastern Washington and north-central Oregon, formally designated on 13 November 1984. It totals about 11 million acres (roughly 4.5 million hectares), with 60,079 acres (24,313 hectares) of vineyard on the Washington side and over 99% of the state's vinifera acreage. Annual rainfall is only 6–8 inches, so irrigation is essential. Loess over gravel and slackwater sediment sits on basalt bedrock. Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Merlot, Riesling and Syrah lead. records.content: Constantia Ward of the Cape Town district in the Western Cape, near False Bay. Simon van der Stel was granted the land in 1685 and named it Constantia; it was divided in 1716 into Groot Constantia, Klein Constantia and Bergvliet. Rainfall is about 1,000 mm and the February mean is 20.6 C, so irrigation is rarely needed. Sauvignon Blanc and other whites are important, and Muscat de Frontignan makes the sweet Vin de Constance. Constantia is a ward, not a district; SAWIS reported the Cape Town statistical area at 2,511 hectares in 2024. Wine of Origin requires 100% origin and 85% for variety and vintage. records.content: Coonawarra A narrow region on the Limestone Coast of South Australia, famous for terra rossa red soil over limestone; a strip about 1.2 km wide and 20 km long is the core of its Cabernet Sauvignon, with GI status in 2003. Coonawarra Coonawarra sits on the Limestone Coast of South Australia and is one of Australia’s defining Cabernet Sauvignon districts. A cigar-shaped ridge of terra rossa red soil lies over ancient limestone, and a cool maritime climate lets the grapes ripen slowly. Fenyang Fenyang is a county-level city administered by Lüliang in Shanxi, located at the western edge of the Jinzhong Basin and beneath the Lüliang Mountains. Xinghuacun lies within Fenyang and is the production place long associated with Fenjiu. Unlike the humid strong-aroma areas of southern Sichuan, Fenyang has a semi-arid monsoon climate with cold winters, windy springs and large temperature swings between day and night. Finger Lakes The Finger Lakes are a cool-climate district of eleven narrow, north-south glacial lakes in upstate New York, part of the United States wine framework. Riesling is the variety best known internationally, while Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc and traditional-method sparkling wine are equally important. records.content: Fujian Province A coastal province in south-east China and an important region for hongqu yellow wine; glutinous rice, red yeast rice and water form the base, with Fuzhou, Longyan and Gutian as representative traditions. Fujian Province Fujian lies on the south-east coast of China, dominated by mountains, hills and a long coastline. In the map of alcoholic drinks its clearest identity is as an important region for hongqu yellow wine: glutinous rice, red yeast rice and water form the material base, and Fuzhou, Longyan and Gutian each developed a distinct tradition. records.content: Fushimi A sake region in Kyoto City's Fushimi ward, known for the Fushui spring water, the Horikawa canal and Jikkokubune boats, and the Gekkeikan and Kizakura brewery museums; in 1889 a Fushimi brewers' tasting drew 35 exhibitors, making it an early arena for ginjo technique. Its water is medium-hard, not purely soft. Fushimi Fushimi is a sake region in the southern part of Kyoto City, centred on the brewery cluster that runs along the Uji River and the Horikawa canal in Fushimi ward. It is not a separate prefecture, nor a vineyard-style legal appellation. Its reputation rests on the Fushui spring water, brewery architecture, and a shipping history that made sake a visible part of the city.

Unlike northern baijiu regions built on sorghum and wheat, Guangdong's drinks tradition follows rice agriculture: rice, glutinous rice and local water underpin rice aroma, soy aroma and sweet yellow rice wine. records.content: Guangxi A karst-and-rice province centred on rice-aroma baijiu, especially Guilin Sanhua, with everyday rice wine and sweet glutinous rice wine alongside. Guangxi Guangxi lies in southern China, bordering Guangdong to the east, Hunan and Guizhou to the north, Yunnan to the west and the Beibu Gulf to the south. Mountains, hills, karst landscapes and river plains interlock; the Li, Liu and Hongshui rivers cut many small basins. Rice farming is the agricultural base, and rice wine is the most everyday drinks tradition. On the national baijiu map, Guangxi's clearest coordinate is rice aroma and Guilin Sanhua. Guizhou Guizhou lies in south-west China, dominated by highlands, mountains and karst landscapes. Its drinks identity is almost inseparable from sauce-aroma baijiu: the Chishui River basin, Maotai town in Renhuai and the hot, humid river valley form the core production area. records.content: Hunan A wet, mountainous province where fuyu and sauce-aroma baijiu coexist with rice wine and yellow rice wine, shaped by the Dongting plain, western valleys and rice farming. Hunan Hunan lies south of the middle Yangtze, ringed by mountains on the east, south and west, and open to the Dongting Lake plain in the north. Wet, mountainous country with dense river networks gives the province a different drinks landscape from the northern plains: high-strength baijiu alongside rice wine, yellow rice wine and local fermented drinks. records.content: Inner Mongolia A northern province of Hetao grain baijiu and grassland fermented mare's-milk wine, with strong aroma on the plain and airag in pastoral life. Inner Mongolia Inner Mongolia stretches across northern China, from the Greater Khingan range in the northeast to the Gobi in the northwest, with grassland, sand, mountains and the Hetao plain. It is not a traditional "baijiu giant", but it has two clear drinks traditions: grain baijiu on the Hetao plain and mare's-milk wine on the grassland. records.content: Ireland An island nation in north-west Europe whose beer tradition is led by dry stout and Irish red ale; Guinness has brewed in Dublin since 1759, with barley, water and hops as the base, and craft brewing has added new styles. Ireland Ireland is an island nation in north-west Europe with a mild, damp climate that suits barley. In the map of alcoholic drinks its clearest identity is as a beer region: dry stout and Irish red ale are the representative styles, and Guinness has brewed in Dublin since 1759. records.content: Islay A whisky island in the Inner Hebrides, about 600 square kilometres in area with a population of roughly 3200. records.content: Italy A major wine-producing country in southern Europe, with vineyards in almost all of its 20 regions; known for native grape varieties, the DOCG/DOC/IGT hierarchy and a range of styles from sparkling wine to bitter aperitifs. Italy Italy is a major wine-producing country in southern Europe, with vineyards in almost all of its 20 regions. Its character is not a single style but a diversity formed by native varieties, local traditions and a classification system: sparkling wine and Nebbiolo at the foot of the Alps in the north, Sangiovese in Tuscany in the centre, and red and sweet wines under the Mediterranean climate of the south and the islands. records.content: Jamaica A Caribbean island country and a major rum region, known for molasses, long fermentation and pot distillation that produce a high-ester, heavy funky style, alongside lighter white rum. Jamaica Jamaica is a Caribbean island country and one of the most important rum regions. records.content: Japan An island country in East Asia best known for sake; shochu, whisky and beer are also established, and sake's specific-name categories are classified by polishing ratio and additives under National Tax Agency labelling rules. Japan Japan is an island country in East Asia whose drinks landscape is centred on sake, alongside shochu, whisky, beer and wine. Sake is made from rice, water, koji and yeast, with saccharification and fermentation running in parallel; shochu and whisky rely on distillation; beer and wine are shaped more by modern industry and imported drinking culture. records.content: Jiangsu Province An eastern coastal province and one of China's important yellow wine regions; Danyang sealed-jar wine uses glutinous rice and wheat qu with sealed ageing for a sweet style, and Wuxi has traditions such as Huiquan wine. Jiangxi Jiangxi lies south of the middle-lower Yangtze, ringed by mountains on the east, south and west, with the Poyang Lake plain in the north. The Gan River runs through the province from south to north. Red soils, hills, rice fields and abundant rain create a classic Jiangnan agricultural landscape and a long base for rice-based brewing. The province's most distinctive baijiu coordinate is Site and te-aroma. records.content: Jimo A glutinous-millet huangjiu region in the southwest of the Shandong Peninsula, now part of Qingdao. Millet, summer-made aged wheat qu and the jiaomi method give a toasted, full-bodied northern huangjiu. Jimo Jimo is in the southwest of the Shandong Peninsula and is now the Jimo District of Qingdao. It is the representative region for northern millet huangjiu. Local production combines millet, summer-made aged wheat qu and the jiaomi method to create a style distinct from the glutinous-rice huangjiu of Shaoxing. records.content: Jura A wine region in eastern France between Burgundy and Switzerland, known for limestone and marl slopes and local varieties such as Savagnin, Poulsard and Trousseau; vin jaune and vin de paille are its signatures, and it also has appellations for red, white and sparkling wines. Jura Jura is a narrow wine region in eastern France, squeezed between Burgundy and the Swiss border. It is best remembered for vin jaune: a white wine made from Savagnin, aged in old oak barrels without topping up or racking, under a film of yeast, for more than six years. Kagoshima Kagoshima is the core honkaku shochu region of southern Kyushu in Japan. records.content: Kentucky A US state and the dominant production area for bourbon, with about 95% of global bourbon supply; known for corn-based mashbills, new charred oak and limestone water, though bourbon is a nationwide US category and Kentucky is not a legal synonym. Kentucky Kentucky lies in the east-central United States and is the most concentrated area of bourbon production. According to the Kentucky Distillers' Association, about 95% of the global bourbon supply comes from here; the state has about 100 licensed distilleries in 42 counties, operated by 84 companies. records.content: Kyoto A prefecture-wide name for sake in Kyoto, divided into Rakuchu, Fushimi, Kyoto Tanba, Miyazu, Fukuchiyama, and Kyotango-Mineyama brewing associations; Rakuchu is represented by small breweries such as Sasaki Shuzo, founded in 1893, and Kyoto sake is closely tied to Kyoto cuisine, temple vegetarian food, and pickles. Kyoto Kyoto is first a Japanese city and also a prefecture. As a sake region, "Kyoto" can mean the breweries inside Kyoto City or the brewing tradition of the whole prefecture. records.content: Luzhou A city at the meeting of the Yangtze and Tuo rivers in southern Sichuan and a core area of Luzhou Laojiao and strong-aroma baijiu; a place to see old cellars, river transport and urban liquor production together. Luzhou Luzhou lies at the south-eastern edge of the Sichuan Basin, where the Yangtze and Tuo rivers meet. Compared with Yibin's river junction, Luzhou feels more like an old Yangtze port: the Tuo brought inland goods, while the Yangtze linked the city with Chongqing and Yibin. Luzhou Laojiao's old cellars are distributed within the urban area, so the distillery and city life sit unusually close together for a Chinese baijiu production centre. In 1851 Silvestre Ochagavía introduced French varieties, the accepted starting point of modern Chilean wine; Concha y Toro was founded in 1883. Peñín records 12,216 hectares, with Cabernet Sauvignon the leading red. The land runs from Andean foothills to coastal hills, with cooler Alto Maipo and ocean-influenced coastal sites. records.content: Margaret River Wine region at the south-west corner of Western Australia, bounded by ocean and highly isolated. The GI covers 2,137 sq km with 5,725 hectares of vineyard (5,840 hectares on the 2024 association basis), from sea level to 234 metres, and 202 mm of growing-season rain. A maritime Mediterranean climate with a small day-night range and even heat accumulation, compared by Wine Australia to Bordeaux in a dry year. Gravelly loam over granite and gneiss has low water-holding capacity. Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Semillon and Sauvignon Blanc lead; the region makes about 2% of the national crush. records.content: Marlborough Marlborough wine region at the north-east end of New Zealand's South Island, the country's largest. The 2026 report records 32,191 hectares planted, 73% of the national total, and 31,603 hectares producing across 1,134 vineyards. Cool but sunny, low rainfall, free-draining moderately fertile soils. Three sub-regions, Wairau Valley, Southern Valleys and Awatere Valley, differ in soil, temperature and wind. Sauvignon Blanc leads, and it opened New Zealand's export market in the 1980s. The Marlborough GI was registered in 2018, and single variety, vintage or region claims require 85%. Martinborough Martinborough is a small, precise wine district at the southern end of the Wairarapa Valley on New Zealand’s North Island, and one of the starting points of the country’s modern Pinot Noir story. Its vineyards are concentrated on the Martinborough Terrace around a compact village, where cool nights, strong winds and free-draining gravels produce wines with a savoury, structural edge. Its distinctive feature is not the scenery but the rules: the French decree of 5 November 1996 created an appellation d'origine contrôlée (AOC) for "Rhum de la Martinique", the first AOC in the rum world to bind both origin and process. records.content: Netherlands A low-lying country in north-west Europe where the Rhine and Meuse reach the sea. records.content: Pessac-Léognan A Bordeaux left-bank AOC split from Graves in 1987, covering ten communes south of the city; known for gravel mounds, both red and white wines and estates such as Haut-Brion and La Mission Haut-Brion, it is Bordeaux’s most urban and accessible fine-wine district. Pessac-Léognan Pessac-Léognan lies south of Bordeaux city, the northern section of the Graves district that became an independent AOC in 1987. Verdejo dominates, at 88.82% of the 2025 harvest; gravel terraces and a wide day-night range shape the high-acid, herbal and citrus style. People remember the list that began in 1955 and overlook two more basic appellation rules: the Saint-Émilion AOC and the Saint-Émilion Grand Cru AOC. records.content: Santorini PDO on the volcanic island of Santorini (Thira) in the Cyclades, Greece, established in 1971. Its dry white must contain at least 85% Assyrtiko, with the remaining 15% limited to Athiri and Aidani. Vineyards cover about 1,200 hectares (12,000 stremmata), from sea level to about 300 metres. Volcanic ash and pumice, extreme drought and the meltemia winds force the kouloura basket system. Maximum yields have been cut from 8,000 to 6,500 kg per hectare; Vinsanto and Nykteri are protected traditional terms. Sauternes Sauternes is the botrytised sweet white appellation of southern Bordeaux, in the Gironde, covering the villages of Sauternes, Barsac, Bommes, Fargues and Preignac. It is not one uniform tract of land but a set of terraces, gravel slopes and clay hollows along the Ciron and the Garonne. records.content: Savoie A wine region in the French Alps of south-east France, with vineyards on valleys and slopes at 250-600 metres; known for white varieties such as Jacquère and Altesse and the red Mondeuse, with appellations including Vin de Savoie, Roussette de Savoie, Crémant de Savoie and Bugey. Savoie Savoie is not a region that can be summed up with an Alpine view. Its vineyards are scattered across valleys, slopes and glacial terraces in south-east France, from 250 metres up to more than 600 metres; two sides of the same mountain can differ completely in soil, aspect and ripening date. records.content: Scotland A legally defined whisky region in the north of the United Kingdom; Scotch whisky must be distilled and matured in Scotland, aged in oak casks for at least three years, bottled at no less than 40% ABV and protected by a geographical indication. Scotland Scotland lies in the north of the United Kingdom and is the legal home of Scotch whisky. Scotch is not just a drink but a protected name and process system: it must be distilled and matured in Scotland, made from water, malted barley (other cereals may be used) and yeast, aged in oak casks for at least three years, and bottled at no less than 40% ABV. records.content: Stellenbosch Wine of Origin district in the Coastal Region of the Western Cape, South Africa, about 45 km east of Cape Town. Its vineyards are about 18% of the national 101,957 hectares, with Simonsberg, Helderberg and granite or sandstone slopes creating diverse terroirs. records.content: United States A major wine, whiskey and beer producer in North America; California, Oregon and Washington form the wine core, Kentucky is known for bourbon, and the AVA system is a distinctive feature of appellation labelling. United States The United States is a major drinks producer in North America, with large-scale wine, whiskey and beer industries. The wine core is in California, while Oregon and Washington have distinctive styles; bourbon from Kentucky is the most representative spirit; beer ranges from industrial lager to a broad craft market. records.content: Valais The largest wine region in Switzerland, spread along the upper Rhône and covering about 32% of the national vineyard area, or some 4,600 hectares; an Alpine valley with about 650 mm of rain and 2,500 hours of sunshine a year and foehn winds, where vines rise to about 1,100 metres at Visperterminen; reds account for 59% and Pinot Noir is the largest variety, alongside Chasselas, known locally as Fendant, Gamay, Petite Arvine, Cornalin and Humagne Rouge; one AOC Valais and ten AOC Grand Cru. Valais Valais, Wallis in German, is the largest wine region in Switzerland, with vineyards along the upper Rhône on both sides of the Alpine valley. Valais photograph Figure: Valais. Photograph: Ful

records.content: Vaud The wine region of the canton of Vaud in Switzerland, with about 3,782 hectares of vineyard and the only Swiss region where white grapes dominate at 65%; Chasselas covers 59%, or about 2,233 hectares, and labels usually give a place name such as Yvorne, Féchy or Dézaley instead of a variety; divided into six sub-regions, Chablais, Lavaux, La Côte, Bonvillars, Côtes de l'Orbe and Vully, with the Lavaux terraces inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2007 and the three Grand Cru appellations Calamin, Dézaley and Dézaley-Marsens. records.content: Veneto A wine region in north-east Italy running from the southern Alps to the Adriatic; represented by Amarone and Ripasso from Valpolicella, Garganega in Soave and Glera in Prosecco, and one of Italy's largest DOC wine-producing regions by volume. Veneto Veneto (Italian Veneto) lies in north-east Italy, running from the Dolomites at the southern edge of the Alps to the Adriatic and the Venetian lagoon. It is a major Italian wine region, best known for three blocks: the red wines of Valpolicella, the whites of Soave and the sparkling wines of Prosecco. Veneto photograph Figure: Veneto. records.content: Vinho Verde The appellation of the Minho region in north-west Portugal, known for fresh, low-alcohol whites shaped by Atlantic influence; in the name, verde refers to youth rather than colour, with a minimum actual alcohol of 8% vol for regular wines, 9% vol when a sub-zone is named and 11.5% vol when Alvarinho is declared, and a maximum total alcohol of 14% vol; the main white varieties are Alvarinho, Loureiro, Arinto, Avesso, Trajadura and Azal, with Vinhão leading the reds. Vinho Verde Vinho Verde is an appellation in the Minho region of north-west Portugal, known for fresh, low-alcohol, high-acid wines. records.content: Vouvray A district east of Tours in the Loire, made entirely from Chenin Blanc and covering dry, off-dry, sweet and sparkling styles; tuffeau limestone caves, a cool climate and its 1936 AOC make it the best place to understand Chenin’s range. Vouvray Vouvray is a white-wine district east of Tours on the right bank of the Loire, with AOC status since 1936. Its principal permitted variety is Chenin Blanc, locally Pineau de la Loire, and one vineyard can be made into dry, off-dry, sweet, botrytised sweet and sparkling styles. Tuffeau limestone plateaus, a cool humid autumn and cave cellars make it the most concentrated place to observe Chenin's range. Vouvray Figure: Vouvray: Vouvray Vineyard

records.content: Walker Bay District in the Cape South Coast region of the Western Cape, around Hermanus. It has three Hemel-en-Aarde wards and Bot River. Cooled by the Benguela Current and sea breezes. Soils are mainly Bokkeveld shale, with granite and Table Mountain sandstone on higher slopes. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay lead, with Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage and Syrah also planted. Tim Hamilton Russell bought 170 hectares in 1975 and released the first vintage in 1981. SAWIS reported Cape South Coast at 2,671 hectares in 2024 with no district figure. Wine of Origin requires 100% origin and 85% for variety and vintage. records.content: Willamette Valley Willamette Valley wine region in north-west Oregon, established as an AVA in 1983. The AVA covers about 3,428,800 acres (1,387,600 hectares), with 25,450 acres (10,300 hectares) of vineyard and about two-thirds of Oregon's wineries. The Coast Range and Cascades shelter a mild, long growing season; soils are marine sedimentary, volcanic and loess. Pinot Noir dominates, first planted in 1965, alongside Pinot Gris, Chardonnay and Riesling. There are 11 nested AVAs, and Oregon requires 90% for a variety label against the federal 75%.
